options.b: b) Sparse array is memory efficient
options.d: d) A naive array is more efficient

mcqs.answer: b) Sparse array is memory efficient
mcqs.explanation: A naive implementation allocates space for the entire size of the array, whereas a sparse array(linked list implementation) allocates space only for the non-default values.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the disadvantage of sparse matrices over normal matrices?
mcqs.explanation: As the sparse matrix contains zeroes  we will compute operations only on non zero values. This increases the complexity of algorithm as we need to identify index of zero elements first and during computation we should not take those index. It is a disadvantage. links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Suffix Array”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is false?

options.a: a) Suffix array is always sorted
options.b: b) Suffix array is used in string matching problems
options.c: c) Suffix array is always unsorted
options.d: d) Suffix array contains all the suffixes of the given string

mcqs.answer: c) Suffix array is always unsorted
mcqs.explanation: Suffix array is always sorted as it contains all the suffixes of a string in sorted order. Suffix arrays are used to solve problems related to string, like string matching problems.

mcqs.question: Suffix array of the string “statistics” is ____________
mcqs.explanation:
The suffix array of the string statistics will be:
2 atistics
8 cs
7 ics
4 istics
9 s
0 statistics
5 stics
1 tatistics
6 tics
3 tistics
In Suffix array, we only store the indices of suffixes. So, correct option is 2 8 7 4 9 0 5 1 6 3.

mcqs.question: Suffix array can be created by performing __________ traversal of a suffix tree.

options.d: d) either breadth-first or level order

mcqs.explanation: A suffix tree is a trie, which contains all the suffixes of the given string as their keys and positions in the string as their values. So, we can construct a suffix array by performing the depth-first traversal of a suffix tree.

mcqs.question: Suffix array is space efficient than the suffix tree.
mcqs.explanation: Suffix arrays are more space efficient than the suffix trees as they just store the original string and an array of integer. But working with suffix tree is faster than that of the suffix array.

mcqs.question: If comparison based sorting algorithm is used construct the suffix array, then what will be time required to construct the suffix array?
mcqs.explanation: On average comparison based sorting algorithms require O(nlogn) comparisons. But comparing a suffix takes O(n). So, overall time to construct the suffix array will be O(nlogn) * O(n) = O(n<sup>2</sup>logn).

mcqs.question: What will be the suffix array of the string “engineering”?
mcqs.explanation:
Correct choice is : 5 0 6 10 2 3 8 4 9 1 7.
Because the suffix array formed will be: 5 eering 0 engineering 6 ering 10 g 2 gineering 3 ineering 8 ing 4 neering 9 ng 1 ngineering 7 ring.

mcqs.question: LCP array and ______ is used to construct suffix tree.
mcqs.explanation: Suffix tree can be created using an LCP array and a suffix array. If we are given a string of length (n + 1) and its suffix array and LCP array, we can construct the suffix tree in linear time i.e in O(n) time.

mcqs.question: What is the time required to locate the occurrences of a pattern P of length m in a string of length n using suffix array?
mcqs.explanation: Suffix arrays are used to find the occurrences of a pattern in a string. Pattern of length m will require m characters to compare, so using suffix array we can find occurrences of a pattern in the string of length n in O(mlogn) time.

mcqs.question: Suffix array can be created in O(nlogn) time.
mcqs.explanation: Suffix array can be constructed in O(n<sup>2</sup>logn) time using sorting algorithms but it is possible to build the suffix array in O(nlogn) time using prefix doubling.

mcqs.question:
Which of the following is/are advantages suffix array one suffix tree? I. Lesser space requirement
II. Improved cache locality
III. Easy construction in linear time

options.b: b) All I, II and III

mcqs.answer: b) All I, II and III
mcqs.explanation: Advantages of the suffix array over suffix tree are : (i) Lesser space requirement (ii) Improved cache locality and (iii) Simple algorithms to construct suffix arrays in linear time.

Solving linear equations is a separate field in Mathematics involving matrices, Image processing stores the pixels in the form of matrices, and the graphs are represented with the help of matrices to indicate the nodes and edges.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an advantage of matrices?

options.b: b) Searching through a matrix is complex

mcqs.explanation: Adjacency and Incidence Matrices are used to store vertices and edges of a graph. It is an advantage to plot graphs easily using matrices. mcqs.question: Matrix A when multiplied with Matrix C gives the Identity matrix I, what is C?
mcqs.explanation: Any square matrix when multiplied with its inverse gives the identity matrix. Note that non square matrices are not invertible.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Sparse Matrix”.

mcqs.question: Which matrix has most of the elements (not all) as Zero?
mcqs.explanation: Sparse Matrix is a matrix in which most of the elements are Zero. Identity Matrix is a matrix in which all principle diagonal elements are 1 and rest of the elements are Zero. Unit Matrix is also called Identity Matrix. Zero Matrix is a matrix in which all the elements are Zero.

mcqs.question: What is the relation between Sparsity and Density of a matrix?

options.c: c) Sparsity = Density*Total number of elements
options.d: d) Sparsity = Density/Total number of elements

mcqs.explanation: Sparsity of a matrix is equal to 1 minus Density of the matrix. The Sparsity of matrix is defined as the total number of Zero Valued elements divided total number of elements.

mcqs.question: Who coined the term Sparse Matrix?
mcqs.explanation: Harry Markowitz coined the term Sparse Matrix. James Sylvester coined the term Matrix. Chris Messina coined the term Hashtag and Arthur Cayley developed the algebraic aspects of a matrix.

mcqs.question: Is O(n) the Worst case Time Complexity for addition of two Sparse Matrix?
mcqs.explanation: In Addition, the matrix is traversed linearly, hence it has the time complexity of O(n) where n is the number of non-zero elements in the largest matrix amongst two.

mcqs.question: The matrix contains m rows and n columns. The matrix is called Sparse Matrix if ________

options.a: a) Total number of Zero elements > (m*n)/2
options.b: b) Total number of Zero elements = m + n
options.c: c) Total number of Zero elements = m/n
options.d: d) Total number of Zero elements = m-n

mcqs.answer: a) Total number of Zero elements > (m*n)/2
mcqs.explanation: For matrix to be Sparse Matrix, it should contain Zero elements more than the non-zero elements. Total elements of the given matrix is m*n. So if Total number of Zero elements > (m*n)/2, then the matrix is called Sparse Matrix.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not the method to represent Sparse Matrix?
mcqs.explanation: Heap is not used to represent Sparse Matrix while in Dictionary, rows and column numbers are used as Keys and values as Matrix entries, Linked List is used with each node of Four fields (Row, Column, Value, Next Node) (2D array is used to represent the Sparse Matrix with three fields (Row, Column, Value).

mcqs.question: Is Sparse Matrix also known as Dense Matrix?
mcqs.explanation: Sparse Matrix is a matrix with most of the elements as Zero elements while Dense Matrix is a matrix with most of the elements as Non-Zero element.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is a Special Sparse Matrix?
mcqs.explanation: A band matrix is a sparse matrix whose non zero elements are bounded to a diagonal band, comprising the main diagonal and zero or more diagonals on either side.

mcqs.question: In what way the Symmetry Sparse Matrix can be stored efficiently?
mcqs.explanation: Since Symmetry Sparse Matrix arises as the adjacency matrix of the undirected graph. Hence it can be stored efficiently as an adjacency list.

mcqs.question: What does the number of inversions in an array indicate?

options.a: a) mean value of the elements of array
options.b: b) measure of how close or far the array is from being sorted
options.c: c) the distribution of values in the array
options.d: d) median value of the elements of array

mcqs.answer: b) measure of how close or far the array is from being sorted
mcqs.explanation: The number of inversions in an array indicates how close or far the array is from being completely sorted. The array is sorted if the number of inversions are 0.

mcqs.question: How many inversions does a sorted array have?
mcqs.explanation: When an array is sorted then there cannot be any inversion in the array. As the necessary condition for an inversion is arr[i]>arr[j] and i<j.

mcqs.question: What is the condition for two elements arr[i] and arr[j] to form an inversion?

options.c: c) arr[i] < arr[j] and i < j
options.d: d) arr[i] > arr[j] and i < j

mcqs.answer: d) arr[i] > arr[j] and i < j
mcqs.explanation: For two elements to form an inversion the necessary condition is arr[i] > arr[j] and i < j. The number of inversions in an array indicate how close or far the array is from being completely sorted.

mcqs.question: Under what condition the number of inversions in an array are maximum?

mcqs.answer: b) when the array is reverse sorted
mcqs.explanation: Number of inversions in an array are maximum when the given array is reverse sorted. As the necessary condition for an inversion is arr[i]>arr[j] and i<j.

mcqs.question: Under what condition the number of inversions in an array are minimum?

mcqs.answer: a) when the array is sorted
mcqs.explanation: Number of inversions in an array are minimum when the given array is sorted. As the necessary condition for an inversion is arr[i]>arr[j] and i<j.

mcqs.question: How many inversions are there in the array arr = {1,5,4,2,3}?
mcqs.explanation: The necessary condition for an inversion is arr[i]>arr[j] and i<j. So there are 5 inversions in the array.

mcqs.question: Which of the following form inversion in the array arr = {1,5,4,2}?
mcqs.explanation: The necessary condition for an inversion is arr[i]>arr[j] and i<j. So there are 3 inversions in the array. These are (5,4), (5,2), (4,2).

mcqs.question: When array reversal and rotation is applied to the same array then the output produced will also be the same every time.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the predefined function for array reversal in C++ ?

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the predefined function for array reversal in javascript?

mcqs.explanation: The predefined function for reversing an array is reverse() in C++ which comes under the library called an algorithm. It requires 2 arguments the first being the pointer to the starting index of the array and the second being the pointer to the last index of the array.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Number of Jumps to Reach End-array Operation”.

mcqs.question: What will be the minimum number of jumps required to reach the end of the array arr[] = {1,3,6,3,6,8,5}?

options.d: d) not possible to reach the end

mcqs.explanation: Each element of the array represents the maximum number of steps that can be taken forward from that element. If the first element is 0 then it is not possible to reach the end.

mcqs.question: What will be the minimum number of jumps required to reach the end of the array arr[] ={0,1,3,6,3,6,8,5}?

options.d: d) not possible to reach the end

mcqs.answer: d) not possible to reach the end
mcqs.explanation: Each element of the array represents the maximum number of steps that can be taken forward from that element. So as the first element here is 0 so we cannot move any further from the first element. Thus, it is not possible to reach the end of the array.

mcqs.question:
What will be the output of the following code? 
#include <bits/stdc++.h> 
using namespace std; 
 
int func(int arr[], int s, int e) 
{
   if (s == e) 
	return 0; 
   if (arr[s] == 0) 
	return INT_MAX; 
 
int min = INT_MAX; 
for (int i = s + 1; i <= e && i <= s + arr[s]; i++) 
{ 
	int jumps = func(arr, i, e); 
	if(jumps != INT_MAX && jumps + 1 < min) 
		min = jumps + 1; 
} 
return min; 
}
 
int main() 
{ 
	int arr[] = {1, 3, 6, 3, 8, 5}; 
	int n = sizeof(arr)/sizeof(arr[0]); 
	cout << func(arr, 0, n-1); 
	return 0; 
}
mcqs.explanation: The given code finds the minimum number of steps required to reach the end of the array by using recursion. So the output will be 3.

mcqs.question:
What will be the output of the following code? 
#include <bits/stdc++.h> 
using namespace std; 
 
int min(int x, int y) 
{ return (x < y)? x: y; } 
 
int func(int arr[], int n) 
{ 
 
	int *jump = new int[n]; 
	int i, j; 
 
	if (n == 0 || arr[0] == 0) 
		return INT_MAX; 
 
	jump[0] = 0; 
 
	for (i = 1; i < n; i++) 
	{ 
		jump[i] = INT_MAX; 
		for (j = 0; j < i; j++) 
		{ 
			if (i <= j + arr[j] && jump[j] != INT_MAX) 
			{ 
				jump[i] = min(jump[i], jump[j] + 1); 
				break; 
			} 
		} 
	} 
	return jump[n-1]; 
} 
 
int main() 
{ 
	int arr[] = {1, 3, 6, 1, 9,7}; 
	int size = sizeof(arr)/sizeof(int); 
	cout<< func(arr,size); 
	return 0; 
}

title: 4. Data Structure MCQ on Types of Lists

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Skip List”.

mcqs.question: What is a skip list?

options.a: a) a linkedlist with size value in nodes
options.b: b) a linkedlist that allows faster search within an ordered sequence
options.c: c) a linkedlist that allows slower search within an ordered sequence
options.d: d) a tree which is in the form of linked list

mcqs.answer: b) a linkedlist that allows faster search within an ordered sequence
mcqs.explanation: It is a datastructure, which can make search in sorted linked list faster in the same way as binary search tree and sorted array (using binary search) are faster.

mcqs.question:
Consider the 2-level skip list
How to access 38?
mcqs.explanation: Let us call the nodes 20, 30, 40 as top lines and the nodes between them as normal lines. the advantage of skip lists is we can skip all the elements between the top line elements as required.

mcqs.question: Skip lists are similar to which of the following datastructure?
mcqs.explanation: Skip lists have the same asymptotic time complexity as balanced binary search tree. For a Balanced Binary Search Tree, we skip almost half of the nodes after one comparison with root element. The same thing done in the skip lists. Hence skip lists are similar to balanced Binary search trees.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity improvement of skip lists from linked lists in insertion and deletion?

options.a: a) O(n) to O(logn) where n is number of elements
options.b: b) O(n) to O(1) where n is number of elements
options.d: d) O(n) to O(n<sup>2</sup>) where n is number of elements

mcqs.answer: a) O(n) to O(logn) where n is number of elements
mcqs.explanation: In Skip list we skip some of the elements by adding more layers. In this the skip list resembles balanced binary search trees. Thus we can change the time complexity from O (n) to O (logn)

mcqs.question: To which datastructure are skip lists similar to in terms of time complexities in worst and best cases?
mcqs.explanation: Skip lists are similar to any randomly built binary search tree. a BST is balanced because to avoid skew tree formations in case of sequential input and hence achieve O(logn) in all 3 cases. now skip lists can gurantee that O(logn) complexity for any input.

mcqs.question: The nodes in a skip list may have many forward references. their number is determined
mcqs.explanation: The number of forward references are determined probabilistically, that is why skip list is a probabilistic algorithm.

mcqs.question:
Are the below statements true about skiplists? In a sorted set of elements skip lists can implement the below operations
i.given a element find closest element to the given value in the sorted set in O(logn)
ii.find the number of elements in the set whose values fall a given range in O(logn)
mcqs.explanation: To achieve above operations augment with few additional stuff like partial counts.

mcqs.question: How to maintain multi-level skip list properties when insertions and deletions are done?

options.a: a) design each level of a multi-level skip list with varied probabilities

mcqs.answer: a) design each level of a multi-level skip list with varied probabilities
mcqs.explanation: For example consider a 2 level skip list. the level-2 skip list can skip one node on a average and at some places may skip 2 nodes, depending on probabilities. this ensures O(logn).

mcqs.question: Is a skip list like balanced tree?
mcqs.explanation: Skip list behaves as a balanced tree with high probability and can be commented as such because nodes with different heights are mixed up evenly.

mcqs.question: What is indexed skip list?

options.a: a) it stores width of link in place of element

mcqs.answer: a) it stores width of link in place of element
mcqs.explanation: The width is defined as number of bottom layer links that are being traversed by each of higher layer elements. e.g: for a level-2 skip lists, all level-1 nodes have 1 as width, for level-2 width will be 2.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Self Organizing List”.

mcqs.question: The self organizing list improves the efficiency of _______
mcqs.explanation: Linear search in a linked list has time complexity O(n). To improve the efficiency of the linear search the self organizing list is used. A self-organizing list improves the efficiency of linear search by moving more frequently accessed elements towards the head of the list.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the Move-To-Front Method for rearranging nodes?

options.a: a) node with highest access count is moved to head of the list
options.c: c) may over-reward infrequently accessed nodes
options.d: d) requires a counter for each node

mcqs.answer: c) may over-reward infrequently accessed nodes
mcqs.explanation: In Move-To-front Method the element which is searched is moved to the head of the list. And if a node is searched even once, it is moved to the head of the list and given maximum priority even if it is not going to be accessed frequently in the future. Such a situation is referred to as over-rewarding.

mcqs.question: What technique is used in Transpose method?

options.a: a) searched node is swapped with its predecessor
options.b: b) node with highest access count is moved to head of the list
options.c: c) searched node is swapped with the head of list
options.d: d) searched nodes are rearranged based on their proximity to the head node

mcqs.answer: a) searched node is swapped with its predecessor
mcqs.explanation: In Transpose method, if any node is searched, it is swapped with the node in front unless it is the head of the list. So, in Transpose method searched node is swapped with its predecessor.

mcqs.question: The worst case running time of a linear search on the self organizing list is ____
mcqs.explanation: Worst case occurs when the element is located at the very end of list. So n comparisons must be made to the locate element. So the worst case running time of linear search on self organizing list is O(n).

mcqs.question: Which of the following data structure is preferred to have lesser search time when the list size is small?
mcqs.explanation: Self-organizing list is easy and simple to implement than search tree and it requires no additional space. So using self organizing list is preferred when list size is small.

mcqs.question: In _____________ method, whenever a node is accessed, it might move to the head of the list if its number of accesses becomes greater than the records preceding it.
mcqs.explanation: In the count method, the number of times a node was accessed is counted and is stored in a counter variable associated with each node. Then the nodes are arranged in descending order based on their access counts. And the node with highest access count is head of the list.

mcqs.question: Symbol tables during compilation of program is efficiently implemented using __________
mcqs.explanation: Self organizing list allows fast sequential search and it is simple to implement and requires no extra storage. Self-organizing list is used to implement the symbol table.

mcqs.question: Which of the following method performs poorly when elements are accessed in sequential order?
mcqs.explanation: Move-to-front method performs poorly when the elements are accessed in sequential order, especially if that sequential order is then repeated multiple times.

mcqs.question: The self organizing list improves _____
mcqs.explanation: The self-organizing list rearranges the nodes based on the access probabilities of the nodes. So the required elements can be located efficiently. Therefore, self-organizing list is mainly used to improve the average access time.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not the rearranging method used to implement self-organizing lists?
mcqs.explanation: Least frequently used is a buffer replacement policy, while other three are methods to reorder the nodes in the self-organizing lists based on their access probability.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Unrolled Linked List”.

mcqs.question: An unrolled linked list consists of which of the following data structures?
mcqs.explanation: An unrolled linked list is a type of linked list, which consists of a linked list with small arrays. It stores an array of fixed size at each node of the list instead of storing just one element. It reduces the memory overhead by using arrays at each node and has the advantage of faster execution of the operations like insertion and deletion due to linked list.

mcqs.question: What happens if a node cannot fit an element in an unrolled linked list?

options.b: b) The elements are moved to the next node

mcqs.answer: b) The elements are moved to the next node
mcqs.explanation: We can implement unrolled linked list through different algorithms. Generally, the lower watermark is set at 50%, which means if a node cannot accommodate more elements, a new node is created and half of the elements of the previous node are inserted in it. It is related to B-tree.

    a.next.elementNum++

However, if the number of elements present in the neighboring node also drops below half of the originally present, we merge both the nodes.

mcqs.question: Insertion and deletion are much faster in an unrolled linked list than in a singly linked list.
mcqs.explanation: As unrolled linked-list has the advantage of fast indexing from the array, searching becomes faster. Hence, in an unrolled linked-list insertion and deletion are much faster compared to a singly linked list as it jumps the entire array at once.

mcqs.explanation: In an unrolled linked list, each node consists of an array of fixed-size elements. It also contains a pointer, which points to the next node in the list. Every node consists of a certain number of maximum elements it can hold.

mcqs.question: Unrolled linked-list requires more storage space for pointers compared to a singly linked list.
mcqs.explanation: Suppose, if we want to store 12 elements, we can use 3 arrays of size 4 at each node. This will require only 3 next pointers whereas a singly linked list will require 12 next pointers in the same case. Hence, an unrolled linked-list requires less storage space for pointers compared to a singly linked list.

mcqs.question: Which of the following represents the space complexity for an unrolled linked list?
mcqs.explanation: An unrolled linked list takes space varying from (n*c/m) to 2(n*c/m). Here, c is the overhead per node, which is constant, m is the number of maximum elements present in an array at the node and n is the total number of nodes. Hence, the space complexity for an unrolled linked list is O(n).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a drawback of an unrolled linked list?
mcqs.explanation: Suppose, we have an unrolled linked list with an array size of 10 at each node. The array is completely filled with elements. Now, if we refer to only a few of the elements present in the array, the memory used to store the rest of the elements will be wasted. This causes a high overhead per node. Hence, the overhead per node is high in an unrolled linked list compared to that of an ordinary linked list.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is the time complexity for inserting an element in an unrolled linked list?
mcqs.explanation: While inserting an element in an unrolled linked list, the list should be maintained in a sorted manner. Hence, we must traverse and find the node in which we want to insert, which takes O(n) time. Hence, the time complexity for inserting an element in an unrolled linked list takes O(n) time.

options.a: a) uses of bitwise XOR operation to decrease storage requirements for doubly linked lists
options.b: b) uses of bitwise XOR operation to decrease storage requirements for linked lists
options.c: c) uses of bitwise operations to decrease storage requirements for doubly linked lists
options.d: d) just another form of linked list

mcqs.answer: a) uses of bitwise XOR operation to decrease storage requirements for doubly linked lists
mcqs.explanation: Why we use bitwise XOR operation is to decrease storage requirements for doubly linked lists.

mcqs.question: What does a xor linked list have?

options.a: a) every node stores the XOR of addresses of previous and next nodes
options.b: b) actuall memory address of next node
options.c: c) every node stores the XOR of addresses of previous and next two nodes
options.d: d) every node stores xor 0 and the current node address

mcqs.answer: a) every node stores the XOR of addresses of previous and next nodes
mcqs.explanation: Every node stores the XOR of addresses.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an advantage of XOR list?

options.b: b) You need to remember the address of the previously accessed node in order to calculate the next node’s address
options.c: c) In some contexts XOR of pointers is not defined
options.d: d) XOR list decreases the space requirement in doubly linked list

mcqs.answer: d) XOR list decreases the space requirement in doubly linked list
mcqs.explanation: XOR linked list stores the address of previous and next nodes by performing XOR operations. It requires single pointer to store both XOR address of next and previous nodes. But the main disadvantages are debugging tools cannot follow XOR chain, previous node address must be remembered to get next nodes and pointers are not defined accurately.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not the properties of XOR lists?

mcqs.question: Where does a triply linked list contains an extra pointer in comparison to a doubly linked list?
mcqs.explanation: Doubly linked list contains a previous and a next pointer, but along with that, a triply linked list also contains an extra pointer at the top of the node, called a top pointer. The value of the top pointer is initialized to null.

mcqs.question: For which of the following purpose a top pointer can be used?

options.a: a) Storing the address of the head pointer
options.b: b) Storing the address of the previous node
options.c: c) Storing the address of the next node
options.d: d) Storing equal values on the same level

mcqs.answer: d) Storing equal values on the same level
mcqs.explanation: The extra pointer in a triply linked list called as a top pointer can be used to store equal values on the same level. If we insert the nodes in the linked list in sorted order, we can store all the equal elements in such a way that they will be on the same level. Hence, they can be accessed by the top pointer.

mcqs.question: A node will be rejected while inserting if the given node is already present in a triply linked list.
mcqs.explanation: At the time of insertion, nodes are to be inserted in a sorted manner. Hence, it is important to find the correct position for the element in the list. If the given node already exists, then the node is inserted at the top of the list.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is the time complexity for inserting at the beginning of a triply linked list?

If we want to insert an element in the front of a triply linked list, we just have to change the addresses of pointers. The following operations are performed:

mcqs.explanation: All the tree data structures given in options are balanced, but B-tree can have more than two children.

mcqs.question: Which of following figures is a balanced binary tree?

options.a: a)
options.b: b)
options.c: c)
options.d: d)

mcqs.answer: b)
mcqs.explanation: In Some tree diagrams, the root of tree has balance factor +2, so the tree is not balanced. If every node in the tree is balanced, then it’s a balanced tree.

mcqs.question: Balanced binary tree with n items allows the lookup of an item in ____ worst-case time.
mcqs.explanation: Searching an item in balanced binary is fast and worst-case time complexity of the search is O(log n).

mcqs.question: Which of the following data structures can be efficiently implemented using height balanced binary search tree?

options.d: d) both sets and priority queue

mcqs.answer: d) both sets and priority queue
mcqs.explanation: Height-Balanced binary search tree can provide an efficient implementation of sets, priority queues.

mcqs.question: Two balanced binary trees are given with m and n elements respectively. They can be merged into a balanced binary search tree in ____ time.
mcqs.explanation: First we store the in-order traversals of both the trees in two separate arrays and then we can merge these sorted sequences in O(m+n) time. And then we construct the balanced tree from this final sorted array.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an advantage of balanced binary search tree, like AVL tree, compared to binary heap?

options.d: d) construction of the tree takes less time than binary heap

mcqs.explanation: Insertion and deletion, in both the binary heap and balanced binary search tree takes O(log n). But searching in balanced binary search tree requires O(log n) while binary heap takes O(n). Construction of balanced binary search tree takes O(nlog n) time while binary heap takes O(n).

mcqs.question: AVL trees are more balanced than Red-black trees.
mcqs.explanation: AVL tree is more balanced than a Red-black tree because AVL tree has less height than Red-black tree given that both trees have the same number of elements.

mcqs.question: The figure shown below is a balanced binary tree. If node P is deleted, which of the following nodes will get unbalanced?
mcqs.explanation: Node U will get unbalanced if node P is deleted, because it’s balance factor will become -2.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Self Balancing Binary Search Tree”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not the self balancing binary search tree?
mcqs.explanation: 2-3-4 Tree is balanced search trees. But it is not a binary tree. So, it is not a self balancing binary tree. AVL tree, Red-Black Tree and Splay tree are self balancing binary search tree.

mcqs.question: The binary tree sort implemented using a self – balancing binary search tree takes ______ time is worst case.
mcqs.explanation: The worst case running time of the binary tree sort is O(n<sup>2</sup>). But, the worst case running time can be improved to the O(n log n) using a self – balancing binary search tree.

mcqs.question: An AVL tree is a self – balancing binary search tree, in which the heights of the two child sub trees of any node differ by _________
mcqs.explanation: In an AVL tree, the difference between heights of the two child sub trees of any node is at most one. If the height differs by more than one, AVL tree performs rotations to balance the tree.

mcqs.question: Associative arrays can be implemented using __________

options.d: d) A self balancing binary search tree

mcqs.answer: d) A self balancing binary search tree
mcqs.explanation: Associative arrays can be implemented using a self balancing binary search tree as the worst-case time performance of self – balancing binary search trees is O(log n).

mcqs.question: Self – balancing binary search trees have a much better average-case time complexity than hash tables.
mcqs.explanation: For lookup, insertion and deletion hash table take O(1) time in average-case while self – balancing binary search trees takes O(log n). Therefore, hash tables perform better in average-case.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a self – balancing binary search tree?
mcqs.explanation: An AA tree, which is a variation of red-black tree, is a self – balancing binary search tree. 2-3 is B-tree of order 3 and Treat is a randomized binary search tree. A threaded binary tree is not a balanced tree.

mcqs.question: A self – balancing binary search tree can be used to implement ________

options.d: d) Priority queue and Heap sort

mcqs.explanation: Self-balancing binary search trees can be used to construct and maintain ordered lists, to achieve the optimal worst case performance. So, self – balancing binary search tree can be used to implement a priority queue, which is ordered list.

mcqs.question: In which of the following self – balancing binary search tree the recently accessed element can be accessed quickly?
mcqs.explanation: In a Splay tree, the recently accessed element can be accessed quickly. In Splay tree, the frequently accessed nodes are moved towards the root so they are quick to access again.

mcqs.question: The minimum height of self balancing binary search tree with n nodes is _____
mcqs.explanation: Self – balancing binary trees adjust the height by performing transformations on the tree at key insertion times, in order to keep the height proportional to log<sub>2</sub>(n).

mcqs.question: Binary tree sort implemented using a self balancing binary search tree takes O(n log n) time in the worst case but still it is slower than merge sort.
mcqs.explanation: The worst case performance of binary tree sort is O(n log n) when it is implemented using a self balancing binary search tree. Self balancing binary search trees perform transformations to balance the tree, which caused balancing overhead. Due to this overhead, binary tree sort is slower than merger sort.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Randomized Binary Search Tree”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a random tree?
mcqs.explanation: Treap, also known as random binary search tree, Random binary tree and Uniform spanning tree are all random tree. Random tree is a tree formed by a random process of addition and deletion of nodes. AVL tree is a self – balanced binary search tree.

mcqs.question: Which process forms the randomized binary search tree?
mcqs.explanation: The randomized binary search tree is formed by the stochastic process. The stochastic process or also called random process is a mathematical tool or object including random variables.

mcqs.question: How many randomized binary search trees can be formed by the numbers (1, 3, 2)?
mcqs.explanation: As there are 3 numbers (1, 3, 2) so total of 6 combinations can be formed using three numbers but Since (2, 1, 3) and (2, 3, 1) are same so in total there are 5 randomized binary search tree that can be formed.

mcqs.question: What is the expected depth of a node in a randomized binary search tree?
mcqs.explanation: The expected value of depth of a node that is for a node a, the expected value of length of path from root to node a is found to be at most 2 log n + O(1).

mcqs.question: What is the longest length path for a node x in random binary search tree for the insertion process?
mcqs.explanation: Although it is difficult to find the length of the longest path in randomized binary search tree, but it has been found that the longest length is around 4.311 log x.

mcqs.question: What is the range of β in finding the length of the longest path in a randomized binary search tree?
mcqs.explanation: The longest path in a randomized binary search tree, but it has been found that the longest length is around 4.311 log x for node x. This is also equal to 1/β log x where β lies in the range (0, 1).

mcqs.question: What is the expected number of leaves in a randomized binary search tree?
mcqs.explanation: In a random mathematical model, the expected value of number of leaves in a randomized binary search tree is found to be exactly (n + 1)/3 using probability.

mcqs.question: Is Treap a randomized tree.
mcqs.explanation: Treap is a type of data structure which is a combination of binary tree and heap. It is an example of a randomized binary search tree. It stores value in pairs.

mcqs.question: What is the probability of selecting a tree uniformly at random?
mcqs.explanation: Catalan number is a sequence of natural number that is used in counting problem. Hence it is found that the selecting off a tree uniformly at random is reciprocal of Catalan number.

mcqs.question: Is mathematical randomized tree can be generated using beta distribution.
mcqs.explanation: Beta distribution can be used using a different shape to generate a randomized binary search tree to create a special type of tree known as a botanical tree.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “AA Tree”.

mcqs.question: AA Trees are implemented using?
mcqs.explanation: AA Trees are implemented using levels instead of colors to overcome the disadvantages of Red-Black trees.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct definition for a horizontal link?

options.a: a) connection between node and a child of equal levels
options.c: c) connection between two child nodes
options.d: d) connection between root node and leaf node

mcqs.answer: a) connection between node and a child of equal levels
mcqs.explanation: A horizontal link is a connection between a node and a child of equal levels.

mcqs.question: How will you remove a left horizontal link in an AA-tree?

options.c: c) by deleting both the elements
options.d: d) by inserting a new element

mcqs.explanation: A left horizontal link is removed by right rotation.  A right horizontal link is removed by left rotation.

mcqs.question: What are the two different operations done in an AA-Tree?
mcqs.explanation: A skew removes a left horizontal link by right rotation and a split removes a right horizontal link by left rotation.

mcqs.question: In an AA-tree, we process split first, followed by a skew.
mcqs.explanation: In an AA-tree, skew is processed first followed by a split.

mcqs.question: How many different shapes does maintenance of AA-Tree need to consider?
mcqs.explanation: An AA-Tree needs to consider only two shapes unlike a red-black tree which needs to consider seven shapes of transformation.

mcqs.question: What is the prime condition of AA-tree which makes it simpler than a red-black tree?

options.a: a) Only right children can be red
options.b: b) Only left children can be red
options.c: c) Right children should strictly be black
options.d: d) There should be no left children

mcqs.answer: a) Only right children can be red
mcqs.explanation: The prime condition of AA-Tree is that only the right children can be red to eliminate possible restructuring cases.

mcqs.question: Which of the following trees is similar to that of an AA-Tree?
mcqs.explanation: AA- Tree is a small variation of Red-Black tree. AA-Trees overcome the complexity faced in performing insertion and deletion in Red-Black Trees.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case analysis of an AA-Tree?
mcqs.explanation: The worst case analysis of an AA-Tree is mathematically found to be O(log N).

mcqs.question: AA-Trees makes more rotations than a red-black tree.
mcqs.explanation: AA- trees make more rotations than a red-black tree since only two shapes are considered for an AA-Tree whereas seven shapes are considered in Red-Black trees.

mcqs.question: Who is the inventor of AA-Tree?
mcqs.explanation: AA-tree is invented by Arne Anderson. Daniel Sleator invented Splay Tree. Rudolf Bayer invented a Red-Black tree. Jon Louis Bentley invented K-d tree.

mcqs.question: What should be the condition for the level of a left node?

options.a: a) It should be less than or equal to that of its parent
options.b: b) It should be greater than that of its parent
options.c: c) It should be strictly less than that of its parent
options.d: d) The level should be equal to one

mcqs.answer: c) It should be strictly less than that of its parent
mcqs.explanation: The level of a left node should be strictly less than that of its parent. The level of a right node is less than or equal to that of its parent.

mcqs.question:
Of the following rules that are followed by an AA-tree, which of the following is incorrect? 1- Only right children can be red
2- Procedures are coded recursively
3- Instead of storing colors, the level of a node is stored
4- There should not be any left children
mcqs.explanation: In an AA-Tree, both left and right children can be present. The only condition is that only right children can be red.

mcqs.question: Comparing the speed of execution of Red-Black trees and AA-trees, which one has the faster search time?

options.c: c) Both have an equal search time

mcqs.explanation: Since an AA-tree tends to be flatter, AA-tree has a faster search time than a Red-Black tree.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “AVL Tree”.

mcqs.question: What is an AVL tree?

options.a: a) a tree which is balanced and is a height balanced tree
options.b: b) a tree which is unbalanced and is a height balanced tree
options.c: c) a tree with three children
options.d: d) a tree with atmost 3 children

mcqs.answer: a) a tree which is balanced and is a height balanced tree
mcqs.explanation: It is a self balancing tree with height difference atmost 1.

mcqs.question: Why we need to a binary tree which is height balanced?

options.a: a) to avoid formation of skew trees
options.c: c) to attain faster memory access

mcqs.answer: a) to avoid formation of skew trees
mcqs.explanation: In real world dealing with random values is often not possible, the probability that u are dealing with non random values(like sequential) leads to mostly skew trees, which leads to worst case. hence we make height balance by rotations.

mcqs.question:
Which of the below diagram is following AVL tree property? i.
ii.

options.d: d) i is not a binary search tree

mcqs.explanation: The property of AVL tree is it is height balanced tree with difference of atmost 1 between left and right subtrees. All AVL trees are binary search tree.

mcqs.question: What is the maximum height of an AVL tree with p nodes?
mcqs.explanation: Consider height of tree to be ‘he’, then number of nodes which totals to p can be written in terms of height as N(he)=N(he-1)+1+N(he-2). since N(he) which is p can be written in terms of height as the beside recurrence relation which on solving gives N(he)= O(logp) as worst case height.

mcqs.question: To restore the AVL property after inserting a element, we start at the insertion point and move towards root of that tree. is this statement true?
mcqs.explanation: It is interesting to note that after insertion, only the path from that point to node or only that subtrees are imbalanced interms of height.

mcqs.question: Given an empty AVL tree, how would you construct AVL tree when a set of numbers are given without performing any rotations?

options.a: a) just build the tree with the given input
options.b: b) find the median of the set of elements given, make it as root and construct the tree
options.d: d) use dynamic programming to build the tree

mcqs.answer: b) find the median of the set of elements given, make it as root and construct the tree
mcqs.explanation: Sort the given input, find the median element among them, make it as root and construct left and right subtrees with elements lesser and greater than the median element recursively. this ensures the subtrees differ only by height 1.

mcqs.question: What maximum difference in heights between the leafs of a AVL tree is possible?

options.a: a) log(n) where n is the number of nodes
options.b: b) n where n is the number of nodes

mcqs.answer: a) log(n) where n is the number of nodes
mcqs.explanation: At every level we can form a tree with difference in height between subtrees to be atmost 1 and so there can be log(n) such levels since height of AVL tree is log(n).

mcqs.question: Why to prefer red-black trees over AVL trees?

options.a: a) Because red-black is more rigidly balanced
options.b: b) AVL tree store balance factor in every node which costs space
options.c: c) AVL tree fails at scale
options.d: d) Red black is more efficient

mcqs.answer: b) AVL tree store balance factor in every node which costs space
mcqs.explanation: Every node in an AVL tree need to store the balance factor (-1, 0, 1) hence space costs to O(n), n being number of nodes. but in red-black we can use the sign of number (if numbers being stored are only positive) and hence save space for storing balancing information. there are even other reasons where redblack is mostly prefered.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Cartesian Tree”.

mcqs.question: What is a Cartesian tree?

options.a: a) a skip list in the form of tree
options.b: b) a tree which obeys cartesian product
options.c: c) a tree which obeys heap property and whose inorder traversal yields the given sequence
options.d: d) a tree which obeys heap property only

mcqs.answer: c) a tree which obeys heap property and whose inorder traversal yields the given sequence
mcqs.explanation: A tree with heap property (parent is either small or big than children) and when traversed in inorder yields the given input sequence. refer below diagram question for clarity.

mcqs.question: Is the below tree representation of 50,100,400,300,280 correct way to represent cartesian tree?
mcqs.explanation: A tree with heap property (parent is either small or big than children) and when traversed in inorder yields the given input sequence is called as a cartesian tree. as the above figure satisies both the properties. note that even min heap tree can be generated. the above is a max heap tree.

mcqs.question:
Which of the below statements are true? i. Cartesian tree is not a height balanced tree
ii. Cartesian tree of a sequence of unique numbers can be unique generated
mcqs.explanation: A height balanced cartesian tree is not possible as seen in above question. also any time a unique sequnce possess a unique cartesian tree, this can be proven through induction.

mcqs.question: What is the speciality of cartesian sorting?

options.a: a) it sorts partially sorted set of data quickly
options.b: b) it considers cartesian product of elements
options.c: c) it sorts elements in less than O(logn)
options.d: d) it is a self balancing tree

mcqs.answer: a) it sorts partially sorted set of data quickly
mcqs.explanation: It can sort a set which requires only some sorting or displacements. for example consider 78, 79, 80, 82, 81, 83, In this only 81 and 82 must be swaped to make it a complete sorted set, in this case cartesian sort comes to the rescue.

mcqs.question: Consider a sequence of numbers to have repetitions, how a cartesian tree can be constructed in such situations without violating any rules?

options.a: a) use any tie-breaking rule between repeated elements
options.b: b) cartesian tree is impossible when repetitions are present
options.c: c) construct a max heap in such cases
options.d: d) construct a min heap in such cases

mcqs.answer: a) use any tie-breaking rule between repeated elements
mcqs.explanation: Consider any of the tie breaking rules, for example the element which appears first can be taken as small among the same elements and then apply cartesian tree rules.

mcqs.question:
What happens if we apply the below operations on an input sequence? i. construct a cartesian tree for input sequence
ii. put the root element of above tree in a priority queue
iii. if( priority queue is not empty) then
iv. search and delete minimum value in priority queue
v. add that to output
vi. add cartesian tree children of above node to priority queue
mcqs.explanation: The above given steps are for sorting a cartesian tree. cartesian sort is benificial in case of partially sorted set of elements. a cartesian sort can be considered as a selection or heap sort maintaing a priority queue.

mcqs.question: Cartesian trees are most suitable for?

options.c: c) minimum range query and lowest common ancestors

mcqs.answer: c) minimum range query and lowest common ancestors
mcqs.explanation:
In a cartesian tree minimum value can be found by finding lowest common ancestor for the extreme elements. consider 11,9,19,16 the lowest element is 9 and is a lowest common ancestor for 11 and 16. and by applying few techniques cartesian tree can be used to even find lowest common ancestors efficiently.
these can be done in constant time. tree can be constructed in linear time (this is the most efficient time for any tree construction) and takes space as many elements are there.

mcqs.question: A treap is a cartesian tree with ___________

options.a: a) additional value, which is a priority value to the key generated randomly
options.b: b) additional value, which is a priority value to the key generated sequentially
options.d: d) additional operations like remove a range of elements

mcqs.answer: a) additional value, which is a priority value to the key generated randomly
mcqs.explanation: A cartesian tree, if feeded with a sorted sequence will generate a straight path (or in tree terminology a skew tree). moreover a cartesian tree basing on same values from the search keys doesnot work well. so a cartesian tree with priority value in addition to search key is called treap.

mcqs.question: Cartesian trees solve range minimum query problem in constant time.
mcqs.explanation: Range minmum query is finding the minimum element in a given subarray of an array. Constant time is achieved by storing the Cartesian trees for all the blocks in the array. Rmq’s are used in string matchings, computing lowest common ancestor and longest common prefix of a sring.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Weight Balanced Tree”.

mcqs.question: What is a weight balanced tree?

options.a: a) A binary tree that stores the sizes of subtrees in nodes
options.b: b) A binary tree with an additional attribute of weight
options.c: c) A height balanced binary tree

mcqs.answer: a) A binary tree that stores the sizes of subtrees in nodes
mcqs.explanation: Unlike AVL and redblack trees which uses height and color as book keeping information, weight balanced trees use the size of subtrees.

mcqs.question: What are the applications of weight balanced tree?

options.a: a) dynamic sets, dictionaries, sequences, maps

mcqs.answer: a) dynamic sets, dictionaries, sequences, maps
mcqs.explanation: They are a type of self balancing trees which are mostly used in storing key-value pairs, which is mostly used in functional programming languages. they are very useful to maintain big set of ordered objects.

mcqs.question: A node of the weight balanced tree has

options.a: a) key, left and right pointers, size

mcqs.answer: a) key, left and right pointers, size
mcqs.explanation: As a weight balanced tree stores height of the subtrees, we need to use size as an additional attribute to every node. also value(for mappings) may be an optional attribute.

mcqs.question:
The size value of various nodes in a weight balanced tree are leaf – zero
internal node – size of it’s two children
is this true?
mcqs.explanation: Size of a node k is size[k] = size[k.left] + 1 + size[k.right] and based on this the weight will be given as weight[k] = size[k] + 1.

mcqs.question: What is the condition for a tree to be weight balanced. where a is factor and n is a node?

options.a: a) weight[n.left] >= a*weight[n] and weight[n.right] >= a*weight[n].
options.b: b) weight[n.left] >= a*weight[n.right] and weight[n.right] >= a*weight[n].
options.c: c) weight[n.left] >= a*weight[n.left] and weight[n.right] >= a*weight[n].
options.d: d) weight[n] is a non zero

mcqs.answer: a) weight[n.left] >= a*weight[n] and weight[n.right] >= a*weight[n].
mcqs.explanation: The tree is said to be a-balanced if the condition is satisfied. and ‘a’ value will be determined during tree formation. large value of ‘a’ is more effective.

mcqs.question: What are the operations that can be performed on weight balanced tree?

options.a: a) all basic operations and set intersection, set union and subset test
options.c: c) set intersection, set union and subset test

mcqs.answer: a) all basic operations and set intersection, set union and subset test
mcqs.explanation: The speciality of a weight balanced tree is a part from basic operations we can perform collective operations like set intersection, which helps in rapid prototyping in functional programming languages.

mcqs.question: Consider a weight balanced tree such that, the number of nodes in the left sub tree is at least half and at most twice the number of nodes in the right sub tree. options.d: d) 50-black root, 18-red left subtree, 100-black right subtree

mcqs.answer: a) 50-black root, 18-red left subtree, 100-red right subtree
mcqs.explanation: Considering all the properties of red-black tree, 50 must be the black root and there are two possibilities for subtrees. one is option “50-black root, 18-red left subtree, 100-red right subtree” and other is making all nodes of the tree to be black.

mcqs.question: What are the operations that could be performed in O(logn) time complexity by red-black tree?

options.a: a) insertion, deletion, finding predecessor, successor

mcqs.answer: a) insertion, deletion, finding predecessor, successor
mcqs.explanation:
We impose restrictions to achieve logarithm time complexities.
impose restrictions are:
. root property is black
. every leaf is black
. children of red node are black
. all leaves have same black.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an application of Red-black trees and why?

options.a: a) used to store strings efficiently
options.b: b) used to store integers efficiently
options.c: c) can be used in process schedulers, maps, sets

mcqs.answer: c) can be used in process schedulers, maps, sets
mcqs.explanation: RB tree is used for Linux kernel in the form of completely fair scheduler process scheduling algorithm. It is used for faster insertions, retrievals.

mcqs.question: When it would be optimal to prefer Red-black trees over AVL trees?

options.a: a) when there are more insertions or deletions
options.b: b) when more search is needed
options.c: c) when tree must be balanced
options.d: d) when log(nodes) time complexity is needed

mcqs.answer: a) when there are more insertions or deletions
mcqs.explanation: Though both trees are balanced, when there are more insertions and deletions to make the tree balanced, AVL trees should have more rotations, it would be better to use red-black. but if more search is required AVL trees should be used.

mcqs.question: Why Red-black trees are preferred over hash tables though hash tables have constant time complexity?

options.a: a) no they are not preferred
options.b: b) because of resizing issues of hash table and better ordering in redblack trees
options.c: c) because they can be implemented using trees

mcqs.answer: b) because of resizing issues of hash table and better ordering in redblack trees
mcqs.explanation: Redblack trees have O(logn) for ordering elements in terms of finding first and next elements. also whenever table size increases or decreases in hash table you need to perform rehashing which can be very expensive in real time. also red black stores elements in sorted order rather than input order.

mcqs.question: How can you save memory when storing color information in Red-Black tree?

options.a: a) using least significant bit of one of the pointers in the node for color information
options.b: b) using another array with colors of each node
options.c: c) storing color information in the node structure
options.d: d) using negative and positive numbering

mcqs.answer: a) using least significant bit of one of the pointers in the node for color information
mcqs.explanation: The node pointers can be used to store color with the help of significant bits. the exceptions of this method are in languages like java where pointers are not used this may not work.

mcqs.question: When to choose Red-Black tree, AVL tree and B-trees?

options.a: a) many inserts, many searches and when managing more items respectively
options.b: b) many searches, when managing more items respectively and many inserts respectively
options.c: c) sorting, sorting and retrieval respectively
options.d: d) retrieval, sorting and retrieval respectively

mcqs.answer: a) many inserts, many searches and when managing more items respectively
mcqs.explanation: Red black when frequent inserts and deletes, AVL when less frequent inserts and deletes, B-tree when using paging from a slow storage device.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Top Tree”.

mcqs.question: Which algorithm is used in the top tree data structure?
mcqs.explanation: Top tree is a type of data structure which is based on unrooted dynamic binary tree and is used to solve path related problems. It allows an algorithm called divide and conquer.

mcqs.question: For how many vertices in a set, is top tree defined for underlying tree?
mcqs.explanation: Top tree is defined for a set having a maximum of 2 vertices for its underlying tree. Those sets having at maximum 2 vertices is called External Boundary Vertices.

mcqs.question: How many edges are present in path cluster?
mcqs.explanation: There are at least 2 edges present in path cluster. Cluster in data structure is defined as the subtree that is connect having maximum of 2 vertices known as Boundary Vertices.

mcqs.question: How many edges does a leaf cluster contain?
mcqs.explanation: If a cluster has no edges and contains only one vertex known as boundary vertex then, it is known as leaf cluster. So a leaf cluster doesn’t contain any edges. It is also known as Point cluster.

mcqs.question: How many edges are present in Edge cluster?
mcqs.explanation: A cluster containing only single edge is known as Edge cluster. So there are in total 1 edge present in edge cluster. Cluster in data structure is defined as the subtree that is connect having maximum of 2 vertices known as Boundary Vertices.

mcqs.question: Which data structure is used to maintain a dynamic forest using a link or cut operation?
mcqs.explanation: Top tree data structure is used to maintain a dynamic forest using link or cut operations. Top tree is a type of data structure which is based on unrooted dynamic binary tree and is used to solve path related problems.

mcqs.question: If A ꓵ B (A and B are two clusters) is a singleton set then it is a Merge able cluster.
mcqs.explanation: If A ꓵ B is a singleton set where A and B are two clusters, that is there are only one node that is common between the clusters then they are known as Merge able cluster.

mcqs.question: Is Top tree used for maintaining Dynamic set of trees called forest.
mcqs.explanation: Top tree data structure is used to maintain a dynamic forest using link or cut operations. Top tree is a type of data structure which is based on unrooted dynamic binary tree and is used to solve path related problems.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for the initialization of top tree?
mcqs.explanation: Generally, trees have weight on its edges. Also there is one to one correspondence of the edges with the top trees. Therefore, top trees can be initialized in O (n) time.

mcqs.question: How many top trees are there in a tree with single vertex?
mcqs.explanation: Tree having a single vertex has no clusters of tree present in the structure. Therefore, there are empty top trees in a tree having a single vertex. Trees with one node are single node.

mcqs.question: Which property makes top tree a binary tree?
mcqs.explanation: Top tree can be considered as a binary tree if the nodes form a cluster, leaves act as an edge and the root of the top tree acts as a tree itself. Then the top tree is called binary tree.

mcqs.question: Which of the dynamic operations are used in Top Tree data structure implementation?
mcqs.explanation: Link returns a single tree having different vertices from top trees. Cut removes the edge from the top tree. Expose is used to implement queries on top trees. Hence all of the options are used as dynamic operations.

mcqs.question: Which of the following are used as an internal operation in Top tree?
mcqs.explanation: Link returns a single tree having different vertices from top trees. Cut removes the edge from the top tree. Expose is used to implement queries on top trees. While merge is an internal operation used to merge two clusters and return as a parent cluster.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for maintaining a dynamic set of weighted trees?
mcqs.explanation: A lot of applications have been implemented using Top tree interface. Maintaining a dynamic set of weighted trees is one such application which can be implemented with O (log n) time complexity.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Splay Tree”.

mcqs.question: What are splay trees?

options.a: a) self adjusting binary search trees
options.d: d) a tree with probability distributions

mcqs.answer: a) self adjusting binary search trees
mcqs.explanation: Splay trees are height balanced, self adjusting BST’s.

mcqs.question: Which of the following property of splay tree is correct?

options.a: a) it holds probability usage of the respective sub trees
options.b: b) any sequence of j operations starting from an empty tree with h nodes atmost, takes O(jlogh) time complexity
options.c: c) sequence of operations with h nodes can take O(logh) time complexity
options.d: d) splay trees are unstable trees

mcqs.answer: b) any sequence of j operations starting from an empty tree with h nodes atmost, takes O(jlogh) time complexity
mcqs.explanation: This is a property of splay tree that ensures faster access. we push the most recently used nodes to top which leads to faster access to recently used values.

mcqs.question: Why to prefer splay trees?

options.c: c) easier to program and faster access to recently accessed items

mcqs.answer: c) easier to program and faster access to recently accessed items
mcqs.explanation: Whenever you insert an element or remove or read an element that will be pushed or stored at the top which facilitates easier access or recently used stuff.

mcqs.question: Is it true that splay trees have O(logn) amortized complexity ?
mcqs.explanation: We go with amortized time complexity when we feel that not all operations are worst and some can be efficiently done. in splay trees not all splay operations will lead to O(logn) worst case complexity.

mcqs.question: What is a splay operation?

options.a: a) moving parent node to down of child
options.b: b) moving a node to root

mcqs.answer: b) moving a node to root
mcqs.explanation: Splay trees mainly work using splay operations. wheneve we insert, delete and search for a node we splay the respective nodes to root. we have zig-zag and zig-zig operations.

mcqs.question: Which of the following options is an application of splay trees?
mcqs.explanation: Splay trees can be used for faster access to recently accessed items and hence used for cache implementations.

mcqs.question: When we have red-black trees and AVL trees that can perform most of operations in logarithmic times, then what is the need for splay trees?

options.a: a) no there is no special usage
options.b: b) In real time it is estimated that 80% access is only to 20% data, hence most used ones must be easily available
options.c: c) redblack and avl are not upto mark
options.d: d) they are just another type of self balancing binary search trees

mcqs.answer: b) In real time it is estimated that 80% access is only to 20% data, hence most used ones must be easily available
mcqs.explanation: May be the stats showing 80-20% may be not accurate, but in real time that is the widely spread scenario seen. If you are into this type of situation, you must choose implementing splay trees.

mcqs.question: After the insertion operation, is the resultant tree a splay tee?
mcqs.explanation: There is a zig-zag and right operation(zig) which gives the right hand side tree. refer splay operations for insertion in splay tree.

mcqs.question:
What output does the below pseudo code produces? 
    Tree_node function(Tree_node x)
    {
        Tree_node y = x.left;
        x.left = y.right;
        y.right = x;
        return y;
    }
mcqs.explanation: When a right rotation is done the parent of the rotating node becomes it’s right node and it’s child becomes it’s left child.

mcqs.question: What is the disadvantage of using splay trees?

options.a: a) height of a splay tree can be linear when accessing elements in non decreasing order.
options.d: d) splay tree performs unnecessary splay when a node is only being read

mcqs.answer: a) height of a splay tree can be linear when accessing elements in non decreasing order.
mcqs.explanation: This will be the case after accessing all n elements in non-decreasing order. Since the height of a tree corresponds to the worst-case access time, this means that the actual cost of an operation can be high. However the amortized access cost of this worst case is logarithmic O(log n).

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Treap”.

mcqs.question: What is the space complexity of a treap algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: The average case and worst case space complexity of a treap is mathematically found to be O(N).

mcqs.question: A treap is a combination of a tree and a heap.
mcqs.explanation: A treap is a combination of a tree and a heap. The structure of a treap is determined by the fact that it is heap-ordered.

mcqs.question: Which is the simplest of all binary search trees?
mcqs.explanation: A treap is the simplest of all binary search trees. Each node is given a numeric priority and implementation is non recursive.

mcqs.question: What is the reason behind the simplicity of a treap?

options.a: a) Each node has data and a pointer
options.b: b) Each node is colored accordingly
options.c: c) It is a binary search tree following heap principles
options.d: d) Each node has a fixed priority field

mcqs.answer: d) Each node has a fixed priority field
mcqs.explanation: A treap is the simplest of all because we don’t have to worry about adjusting the priority of a node.

mcqs.question: What is the condition for priority of a node in a treap?

options.a: a) a node’s priority should be greater than its parent
options.b: b) a node’s priority should be at least as large as its parent
options.c: c) the priority is randomly assigned and can have any value
options.d: d) a node’s priority is always given in decreasing order

mcqs.answer: b) a node’s priority should be at least as large as its parent
mcqs.explanation: A node’s priority should satisfy heap order. That is, any node’s priority should be at least as large as its parent.

mcqs.question: Several other operations like union set difference and intersection can be done in treaps.
mcqs.explanation: Other than insertion, deletion and search operations, several operations like union, intersection and set difference can be done in treaps.

mcqs.question: What is the average running time of a treap?
mcqs.explanation: The average case and worst case analysis of a treap are mathematically found to be O(log N).

mcqs.question: Which node has the lowest priority in a treap?
mcqs.explanation: A root node has the lowest priority in a treap since the node’s priority is based on heap order.

mcqs.question: What is the priority of a null node?
mcqs.explanation: The priority of a null node is set to be infinity in a treap so that during deletion, priority of that particular node is set to infinity, rotated and freed.

mcqs.question: Who invented treaps?
mcqs.explanation: Cecilia and Raimund invented Treaps. Arne Andersson invented AA – Trees. Donald Shell invented shell sort and Harris and Ross formulated maximum flow problem.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Threaded Binary Tree”.

mcqs.question: What is a threaded binary tree traversal?

options.a: a) a binary tree traversal using stacks
options.b: b) a binary tree traversal using queues
options.c: c) a binary tree traversal using stacks and queues
options.d: d) a binary tree traversal without using stacks and queues

mcqs.answer: d) a binary tree traversal without using stacks and queues
mcqs.explanation: This type of tree traversal will not use stack or queue.

mcqs.question: What are the disadvantages of normal binary tree traversals?

options.a: a) there are many pointers which are null and thus useless
options.b: b) there is no traversal which is efficient

mcqs.answer: a) there are many pointers which are null and thus useless
mcqs.explanation: As there are majority of pointers with null value going wasted we use threaded binary trees.

mcqs.question: In general, the node content in a threaded binary tree is ________

options.a: a) leftchild_pointer, left_tag, data, right_tag, rightchild_pointer

mcqs.answer: a) leftchild_pointer, left_tag, data, right_tag, rightchild_pointer
mcqs.explanation: It contains additional 2 pointers over normal binary tree node structure.

mcqs.question: What are null nodes filled with in a threaded binary tree?

options.a: a) inorder predecessor for left node and inorder successor for right node information
options.b: b) right node with inorder predecessor and left node with inorder successor information

mcqs.answer: a) inorder predecessor for left node and inorder successor for right node information
mcqs.explanation: If preorder or postorder is used then the respective predecessor and successor info is stored.

mcqs.question: Which of the following tree traversals work if the null left pointer pointing to the predecessor and null right pointer pointing to the successor in a binary tree?
mcqs.explanation: In threaded binary trees, the null left pointer points to the predecessor and the right null pointer point to the successor. In threaded binary trees, we can use in-order, preorder and postorder traversals to visit every node in the tree.

mcqs.question: What are double and single threaded trees?

options.a: a) when both left, right nodes are having null pointers and only right node is null pointer respectively
options.c: c) using single and double linked lists
options.d: d) using heaps and priority queues

mcqs.answer: a) when both left, right nodes are having null pointers and only right node is null pointer respectively
mcqs.explanation: They are properties of double and single threaded binary trees respectively.

mcqs.question:

options.a: a) inordersuccessor instead of inorderpredecessor must be done

mcqs.question: What is inefficient with the below threaded binary tree picture?
