links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Tango Tree”.

mcqs.question: Who developed the concept of tango tree?
mcqs.explanation: Erik Demaine is a well-known professor of Computer Science at MIT. John Lacono is an American computer scientist specialized in data structure and algorithm while Mihai Patrascu was a Romanian- American computer scientist. All of them together developed the concept of Tango tree.

mcqs.question: Which type of tree is tango tree?
mcqs.explanation: Tango tree is an example of binary search tree which was developed by four famous scientists Erik Demaine, Mihai Patrascu, John Lacono and Harmon in the year 2004.

mcqs.question: After which city is tango tree named?
mcqs.explanation: Tango is a popular couple dance or partner dance that was originated in the 1880s somewhere between Argentina and Uruguay. Buenos Aires is a capital city off Argentina. Hence they named after Buenos Aires.

mcqs.question: Which type of binary search tree or algorithm does tango tree use?
mcqs.explanation: Tango tree is an online binary search tree whose time complexity is O (log (log n)) when compared to the time complexity of offline binary search tree model. Online algorithm processes input or data provided piece by piece.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of for achieving competitive ratio by tango tree?
mcqs.explanation: Tango tree is an online binary search tree whose time complexity is O (log (log n)) when compared to the time complexity of offline binary search tree model. Online algorithm processes input or data provided piece by piece.

mcqs.question: Which type of binary search tree is imitated for construction of tango tree?
mcqs.explanation: Tango tree is constructed by simulating a complete binary search tree. This tree is also known as Reference tree, that contains all the elements of the tree. Also, the reference tree is never showed in actual implementation.

mcqs.question: Which special balanced binary search tree is used to store the nodes of auxiliary tree?
mcqs.explanation: The path starting from the root and following the path of preferred child node till the end of leaf node is known as preferred path. Nodes are stored in Red – Black tree for the representation of the preferred path.

mcqs.question: Is tango tree represented as a tree of trees.
mcqs.explanation: Partitioning method is used by tango tree which partitions a binary search tree into small sets of paths and then storing them to auxiliary trees. Hence tango tree is represented as a tree of trees.

mcqs.question: Which operation is used to combine two auxiliary trees?
mcqs.explanation: If the top node of one of the reference tree amongst the two, is the is the child of the bottom node of the other reference tree, then the join operation can be carried out to join the two auxiliary trees.

mcqs.question: Is partitioning method used by Tango Tree.
mcqs.explanation: Partitioning method is used by tango tree which partitions a binary search tree into small sets of paths and then storing them to auxiliary trees. Hence tango tree is represented as a tree of trees.

mcqs.question: Which operation is used to break a preferred path into two sets of parts at a particular node?
mcqs.explanation: A preferred path is broken into two parts. One of them is known as top part while other is known as bottom part. To break a preferred path into two sets, cut operation is used at a particular node.

mcqs.question: What is the upper bound for a tango tree if k is a number of interleaves?
mcqs.explanation: Upper bound is found to analyze the work done by a tango tree on a given set of sequences. In order to connect to the tango tree, the upper bound is found to be k+1 O (log (log n)).

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for searching k+1 auxiliary trees?
mcqs.explanation: Since each search operation in the auxiliary tree takes O (log (log n)) time as auxiliary tree size is bounded by the height of the reference tree that is log n. So for k+1 auxiliary trees, total search time is k+1 O (log (log n)).

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for the update cost on auxiliary trees?
mcqs.explanation: The update cost also is bounded by the upper bound. We perform one cut as well as one join operation for the auxiliary tree, so the total update cost for the auxiliary tree is found to be k+1 O (log (log n)).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the self-adjusting binary search tree?
mcqs.explanation: Splay tree is a self – adjusting binary search tree. It performs basic operations on the tree like insertion, deletion, loop up performing all these operations in O (log n) time.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Rope”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is also known as Rope data structure?
mcqs.explanation: Array is a linear data structure. Strings are a collection and sequence of codes, alphabets or characters. Linked List is a linear data structure having a node containing data input and the address of the next node. The cord is also known as the rope data structure.

mcqs.question: Which type of data structure does rope represent?
mcqs.explanation: Rope is a special binary tree in which the end nodes contain the string and its length. The array is a linear data structure. Linked List is a linear data structure having a node containing data input and the address of the next node. The queue is a data structure working on the principle of FIFO.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for finding the node at x position where n is the length of the rope?
mcqs.explanation: In order to find the node at x position in a rope data structure where N is the length of the rope, we start a recursive search from the root node. So the time complexity for worst case is found to be O (log N).

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for creating a new node and then performing concatenation in the rope data structure?
mcqs.explanation: In order to perform the concatenation on the rope data structure, one can create two nodes S1 and S2 and then performing the operation in constant time that is the time complexity is O (1).

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for splitting the string into two new string in the rope data structure?
mcqs.explanation: In order to perform the splitting on the rope data structure, one can split the given string into two new string S1 and S2 in O (log n) time. So, the time complexity for worst case is O (log n).

mcqs.question: Which type of binary tree does rope require to perform basic operations?
mcqs.explanation: To perform the basic operations on a rope data structure like insertion, deletion, concatenation and splitting, the rope should be a balanced tree. After performing the operations one should again re-balance the tree.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for inserting the string and forming a new string in the rope data structure?
mcqs.explanation: In order to perform the insertion on the rope data structure, one can insert the given string at any position x to form a new string in O (log n) time. So, the time complexity for worst case is O (log n). This can be done by one split operation and two concatenation operations.

mcqs.question: Is insertion and deletion operation faster in rope than an array?
mcqs.explanation: In order to perform the insertion on the rope data structure, the time complexity is O (log n). In order to perform the deletion on the rope data structure, the time complexity for worst case is O (log n). While for arrays the time complexity is O (n).

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for deleting the string to form a new string in the rope data structure?
mcqs.explanation: In order to perform the deletion on the rope data structure, one can delete the given string at any position x to form a new string in O (log n) time. So, the time complexity for worst case is O (log n). This can be done by two split operations and one concatenation operation.

mcqs.question: Is it possible to perform a split operation on a string in the rope if the split point is in the middle of the string.
mcqs.explanation: In order to perform the splitting on the rope data structure, one can split the given string into two new string S1 and S2 in O (log n) time. So, the time complexity for worst case is O (log n). The split operation can be performed if the split point is either at the end of the string or in the middle of the string.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “B-Tree”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most widely used external memory data structure?

options.d: d) Both AVL tree and Red-black tree

mcqs.explanation: In external memory, the data is transferred in form of blocks. These blocks have data valued and pointers. And B-tree can hold both the data values and pointers. So B-tree is used as an external memory data structure.

mcqs.question: B-tree of order n is a order-n multiway tree in which each non-root node contains __________
mcqs.explanation: A non-root node in a B-tree of order n contains at least (n – 1)/2 keys. And contains a maximum of (n – 1) keys and n sons.

mcqs.question: A B-tree of order 4 and of height 3 will have a maximum of _______ keys.
mcqs.explanation: A B-tree of order m of height h will have the maximum number of keys when all nodes are completely filled. So, the B-tree will have n = (m<sup>h+1</sup> – 1) keys in this situation. So, required number of maximum keys = 4<sup>3+1</sup> – 1 = 256 – 1 = 255.

mcqs.question: Five node splitting operations occurred when an entry is inserted into a B-tree. Then how many nodes are written?
mcqs.explanation: If s splits occur in a B-tree, 2s + 1 nodes are written (2 halves of each split and the parent of the last node split). So, if 5 splits occurred, then 2 * 5 + 1, i.e. 11 nodes are written.

mcqs.question: B-tree and AVL tree have the same worst case time complexity for insertion and deletion.
mcqs.explanation: Both the B-tree and the AVL tree have O(log n) as worst case time complexity for insertion and deletion.

mcqs.question: 2-3-4 trees are B-trees of order 4. They are an isometric of _____ trees.
mcqs.explanation: 2-3-4 trees are isometric of Red-Black trees. It means that, for every 2-3-4 tree, there exists a Red-Black tree with data elements in the same order.

mcqs.question: Figure shown below is B-tree of order 5. What is the result of deleting 130 from the tree?

options.a: a)
options.b: b)
options.c: c)
options.d: d)

mcqs.answer: c)
mcqs.explanation: Each non-root in a B-tree of order 5 must contain at least 2 keys. Here, when the key 130 is deleted the node gets underflowed i.e. number of keys in the node drops below 2. So we combine the node with key 110 with it’s brother node having keys 144 and 156. And this combined node will also contain the separator key from parent i.e. key 140, leaving the root with two keys 110 and 160.

mcqs.question: What is the best case height of a B-tree of order n and which has k keys?
mcqs.explanation: B-tree of order n and with height k has best case height h, where h = logn (k+1) – 1. The best case occurs when all the nodes are completely filled with keys.

mcqs.question: Compression techniques can be used on the keys to reduce both space and time requirements in a B-tree.
mcqs.explanation: The front compression and the rear compression are techniques used to reduce space and time requirements in B-tree. The compression enables to retain more keys in a node so that the number of nodes needed can be reduced.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is true?

options.a: a) larger the order of B-tree, less frequently the split occurs
options.b: b) larger the order of B-tree, more frequently the split occurs
options.c: c) smaller the order of B-tree, more frequently the split occurs
options.d: d) smaller the order of B-tree, less frequently the split occurs

mcqs.answer: a) larger the order of B-tree, less frequently the split occurs
mcqs.explanation: The average probability of the split is 1/(⌈m / 2⌉ – 1), where m is the order of B-tree. So, if m larger, the probability of split will be less.

mcqs.question: A B+ tree can contain a maximum of 7 pointers in a node. What is the minimum number of keys in leaves?

And In a B+tree –  i)The path from the root to every leaf node is of the same length, so the tree is balanced. ii) Leaves are linked, so allow sequential searching. iii) An index is built with a single key per block of data rather than with one key per data record, so it is shallower than B-tree.

mcqs.question: What will be the time complexity of query operation if all the candidates are evenly spaced so that each bin has constant no. of candidates? (k = number of bins query rectangle intersects)
mcqs.explanation: The process of query becomes faster in a case when the number of candidates are equally distributed among the bins. In such a case the query operation becomes O(k).

mcqs.question: What will be the time complexity of delete operation if all the candidates are evenly spaced so that each bin has constant no. of candidates? (m = number of bins intersecting candidate intersects)
mcqs.explanation: The process of deletion becomes faster in a case when the number of candidates are equally distributed among the bins. In such a case the query operation becomes O(m). It is practically slower than insertion in this case.

mcqs.question: What will be the time complexity of insertion operation if all the candidates are evenly spaced so that each bin has constant no. of candidates? (m = number of bins intersecting candidate intersects)
mcqs.explanation: The process of insertion becomes faster in the case when the number of candidates are equally distributed among the bins. In such a case the query operation becomes O(m). It is practically faster than deletion in this case.

mcqs.question: Efficiency of bin depends upon ___________

options.a: a) size of query and candidates
options.b: b) location of query and candidates
options.c: c) location and size of query and candidates

mcqs.answer: c) location and size of query and candidates
mcqs.explanation: Efficiency of bin depends upon the location and size of query and candidates. It is similar to that of a hash table.

mcqs.question: Bigger the query rectangle the better is the query efficiency.
mcqs.explanation: Efficiency of bin depends upon the location and size of query and candidates. Also, the smaller is the query rectangle the better is the query efficiency.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “KD Tree”.

mcqs.question: In what time can a 2-d tree be constructed?
mcqs.explanation: A perfectly balanced 2-d tree can be constructed in O(N log N) time. This value is computed mathematically.

mcqs.question: Insertion into a 2-d tree is a trivial extension of insertion into a binary search tree.
mcqs.explanation: Insertion of elements in a 2-d tree is similar to that of a binary search tree. Hence, it is a trivial extension of the binary search tree.

mcqs.question: In a two-dimensional search tree, the root is arbitrarily chosen to be?
mcqs.explanation: In a two- dimensional k-d tree (i.e.) 2-d tree, the root is arbitrarily chosen to be an odd level and it applies to all 2-d trees.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the simplest data structure that supports range searching?
mcqs.explanation: K-d trees are the simplest data structure that supports range searching and also it achieves the respectable running time.

mcqs.question: In a k-d tree, k originally meant?
mcqs.explanation: Initially, 2-d trees were created. Then, 3-d trees, 4-trees etc., where k meant the number of dimensions.

mcqs.question: What will be the correct sequence of insertion for the following k-d tree?
mcqs.explanation: The correct sequence of insertion of the above given tree is (30,40),(5,25),(10,12),(70,70),(50,30),(35,45). The insertion is given by, first left, then right.

mcqs.question: Each level in a k-d tree is made of?
mcqs.explanation: Each level in a k-d tree is made of dimensions and cutting. Cutting and dimensions are used for insertion, deletion and searching purposes.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case of finding the nearest neighbour?
mcqs.explanation: The worst case analysis of finding the nearest neighbour in a k-d tree is mathematically found to be O(N).

mcqs.question: What is the run time of finding the nearest neighbour in a k-d tree?
mcqs.explanation: The run time of finding the nearest neighbour in a kd tree is given as O(2<sup>d</sup> log N) where 2<sup>d</sup> is the time taken to search the neighbourhood.

mcqs.question: How many prime concepts are available in nearest neighbour search in a kd tree?
mcqs.explanation: Three important concepts are available in finding the nearest neighbour. They are partial results, pruning, traversal order.

mcqs.question: Reducing search space by eliminating irrelevant trees is known as?
mcqs.explanation: Pruning is eliminating irrelevant trees. Partial results are keeping best results and updating. Traversal is visiting all the nodes of a tree.

mcqs.question: Several kinds of queries are possible on a k-d called as?
mcqs.explanation: Several range queries are possible on a k-d tree. One of the range queries is known as a partial match query.

mcqs.question: What is the time taken for a range query for a perfectly balanced tree?
mcqs.explanation: For a perfectly balanced k-d tree, the range query could take O(√N+M) in the worst case to report M matches.

mcqs.question: The 2d search tree has the simple property that branching on odd levels is done with respect to the first key.
mcqs.explanation: Branching on odd levels is done with respect to the first key and branching on even levels is done with respect to the second key in a 2-d tree.

mcqs.question: Who invented k-d trees?
mcqs.explanation: Jon Bentley found k-d trees. Rudolf Bayer found red black trees. Arne Andersson found AA- trees.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Abstract Syntax Tree”.

mcqs.question: Which tree traversal technique is used to evaluate the expression represented by syntax tree?
mcqs.explanation: Post-order traversal is used to navigate the syntax tree in order to evaluate the expression represented by the tree. It starts from the root node and visits the children of each node from left to right recursively. It is a special case of depth first traversal.

mcqs.question: Which pattern is used to evaluate abstract syntax tree?
mcqs.explanation: Visitor pattern allows you to add methods to classes of different types without alteration to those classes. It also allows you to define external classes that can extend other classes. Visitor pattern is used to evaluate abstract syntax tree.

mcqs.question: Abstract syntax tree is an input to which phase of compiler?
mcqs.explanation: An abstract syntax tree is the output of the parser, the second phase i.e. syntax analysis and it forms an input to semantic analysis phase of the compiler. To determine semantic correctness of declarations and statements written in program, semantic analysis is performed.

mcqs.question: Which of the following expression can be represented by the given syntax tree?
mcqs.explanation:
Step-1: Evaluating the left sub-tree: Since, no operation is performed the value is 7.
Step-2: Evaluating the right sub-tree: (3 * 5)
Step-3: Applying the root operation: 7 + (3 * 5)

mcqs.question: In an abstract syntax tree, each internal node represents an operand and each leaf node represents  an operator.
mcqs.explanation: For an expression represented by an abstract syntax tree, each internal node represents an operator. The operands of the operator are represented by the children of the node. A grammar rule can’t be represented by an internal node in syntax tree.

mcqs.question: Consider the given syntax tree. Assume that division has the lowest precedence than addition, subtraction and multiplication. Addition and subtraction have the same precedence but more than multiplication. Which of the following expression can be given by the following syntax tree?
mcqs.explanation: The root represents the operator /. The subtrees of the root represent the subexpressions 5, (p + q) and (q – r). The grouping of (p + q) and (q – r) as an operand reflects the left to right evaluation of the operators at the same precedence level. Since +, – have the same precedence and * has higher precedence p + q * q – r is equivalent to (p + q) * (q – r). The correct expression is [5 / (p + q) * (q – r)].

mcqs.question: Syntax trees are comparatively denser than parse trees.
mcqs.explanation: Syntax trees are called abstract syntax trees because they do not represent all the precise information from the real syntax of the program. Syntax trees are dense in comparison with parse tree, for constructing the same language.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an application of abstract syntax tree?

options.c: c) Used for dynamic memory allocation
options.d: d) To represent networks of communication

mcqs.explanation: Abstract syntax trees are used to analyze static code whereas B-trees are used to implement indexing in the database. Dynamic memory allocation is the application of linked list and graph is used to represent networks of communication.

mcqs.question: Which parsing approach is followed by syntax tree?
mcqs.explanation: Abstract Syntax Tree follows bottom-up parsing, it is the process of reducing the input string to start symbol. The syntax tree is constructed starting from the non-terminals and ends on the start symbol. To reach the start symbol, we apply production rules to find a rightmost derivation of string in reverse manner.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Parse Tree”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is correct with respect to a parse tree for a given grammar?

options.a: a) n parse tree = n leftmost derivation tree = n rightmost derivation tree
options.b: b) n parse tree = n leftmost derivation tree
options.c: c) n parse tree = n rightmost derivation tree
options.d: d) n parse tree = n non-terminals

mcqs.answer: a) n parse tree = n leftmost derivation tree = n rightmost derivation tree
mcqs.explanation: For a given string, if more than one parse tree exists, then their equivalent leftmost derivation tree and rightmost derivation tree also exists. A grammar that generates more than one parse tree is called an ambiguous grammar.

mcqs.question: Which data structure is used in the syntax analysis phase of the compiler?
mcqs.explanation: Tree data structure in the form of a parse tree is used in the syntax analysis phase of the compiler. It is used to represent the source program in compiler. The given input string and pre-defined grammar are used to construct the parse tree.

mcqs.question: Parse tree for the expression p & q % r % s & t & u is given below. Which of the following is correct for the given parse tree?
mcqs.explanation: According to the given parse tree, % will be evaluated first. So % has higher precedence than & and is left-associative. In the sub-expression s & t & u, (t & u) will be evaluated first. Hence, & is right-associative and has lower precedence than %.

mcqs.question:
Suppose X is the starting symbol of the given grammar with the following transition rules. Compute the value of X as the root of the parse tree for the expression: 3 & 4 % 7. X → X1 & B | B {X.value = X1.value + B.value, X.value = B.value}
B → B1 % D | D {B.value = B1.value * D.value, B.value = D.value}
D → num {D.value = num.value}
mcqs.explanation: According to the semantic rules given in the question, & is equivalent to + and % is equivalent to *. * has higher precedence than +, because % is far from the starting symbol. Both % and & are left-associative. Hence, we can solve the expression as (3 + (4 * 7)) = 31.

mcqs.question: In parse trees, every internal node represents a non-terminal and every leaf node represents a terminal.
mcqs.explanation: For an expression represented by a parse tree, every internal node represents a grammar rule. Terminals are represented by the children of the node. The right-hand side of any production in grammar is represented by the children of a node.

mcqs.question: Consider two arithmetic operators + and –. The precedence of + is higher than that of –. + is right-associative whereas – is left-associative. Which of the following parse tree represents the expression (2 – 4 + 6 + 8 -1)?

options.a: a)
options.b: b)
options.c: c)
options.d: d)

mcqs.answer: a)
mcqs.explanation: + has the highest precedence, the sub-expression (4 + 6 + 8) will be evaluated first. Since + is right associative, 6 + 8 will be evaluated first. Hence, the expression will be evaluated as ((2 – (4 + (6 + 8))) – 2).

mcqs.question: Parse tree is constructed from the tokens produced by lexical analyzer.
mcqs.explanation: Lexical analyzer generates token streams as output and is given to syntax analyzer as input. Here the source code is analyzed and using the input string and the production rules parse tree is constructed.

mcqs.question: Assume +, -, * are usual arithmetic operators. * has the lowest precedence, + has the highest precedence and the precedence of – is medium. + and * are left-associative whereas – is right-associative. What is the value of the expression 3 – 8 + 2 – 9 * 3?
mcqs.explanation:
+ has the highest precedence.
= 3 – 8 + 2 – 9 * 3
= 3 – 10 – 9 * 3
= 3 – 1 * 3
= 2 * 3
= 6
Hence, the value of the given expression is 6.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best represents the computational complexity of GLR parsing?
mcqs.explanation: The best computational complexity of GLR parsing is given by the Tomita parsing algorithm. Let us consider that |G| is the size of the grammar and n is the length of the string to be parsed, then the maximum time required by the algorithm is O(|G| x n). It is an adaption of Knuth’s algorithm.

mcqs.question: While evaluating the parse tree, which traversal technique is used to give the original input string?
mcqs.explanation: To evaluate an expression in the parse tree, in-order traversal technique is used to give the original input string. The precedence of the operators is followed by a parse tree. The operator in the sub-tree has higher precedence than the operator in the parent node. Hence, the innermost sub-tree is evaluated first.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Expression Tree”.

mcqs.question: The leaves of an expression tree always contain?
mcqs.explanation: The leaves of an expression tree always contain the result of a given expression (i.e.) operands.

mcqs.question: A node can have a minimum of one child.
mcqs.explanation: It is possible for a node to have at least one child, as is the case with the unary minus operator.

mcqs.question: What does the other nodes of an expression tree(except leaves) contain?
mcqs.explanation: The nodes other than leaves always contain only operators. There cannot be any operand in those nodes.

mcqs.question: An expression tree is a kind of?
mcqs.explanation: The expression tree is a binary tree. It contains operands at leaf nodes and remaining nodes are filled with operators. The operands and the operators can be arranged in any order (ascending, descending).

mcqs.question: The expression obtained by recursively producing a left expression, followed by an operator, followed by recursively producing a right expression is called?
mcqs.explanation: It is an infix expression because the format of an infix expression is given by operand-operator-operand.

mcqs.question: The average depth of a binary tree is given as?
mcqs.explanation: The average depth of a binary expression tree is mathematically found to be O(√N).

mcqs.question: Only infix expression can be made into an expression tree.
mcqs.explanation: All infix, prefix and postfix expressions can be made into an expression tree using appropriate algorithms.

mcqs.question: An expression tree is created using?
mcqs.explanation: A postfix expression is converted into an expression tree by reading one symbol at a time and constructing a tree respectively.

mcqs.question: ++a*bc*+defg is an?
mcqs.explanation: It is a prefix expression obtained from a preorder traversal since it is of the form operator-operand-operand.

mcqs.question: An expression tree’s nodes can be deleted by calling?
mcqs.explanation: In Binary trees, nodes are created by calling malloc and they are deleted by calling free.

mcqs.question: What is the postfix expression for the following expression tree?
mcqs.explanation: If the given expression tree is evaluated, the postfix expression ab+cde+** is obtained.

mcqs.question: In an expression tree algorithm, what happens when an operand is encountered?

options.a: a) create one node pointing to a stack
options.b: b) pop the nodes from the stack

mcqs.answer: a) create one node pointing to a stack
mcqs.explanation: When an operand is encountered, create one node trees and push it on to the stack. When an operator is encountered, pop the pointers from last two trees from the stack.

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Heap”.

mcqs.question: In a max-heap, element with the greatest key is always in the which node?

options.b: b) First node of left sub tree
options.d: d) First node of right sub tree

mcqs.explanation: This is one of the property of max-heap that root node must have key greater than its children.

mcqs.question: Heap exhibits the property of a binary tree?
mcqs.explanation: Yes, because the leaf nodes are present at height h or h-1, which is a property of complete binary tree.

mcqs.question: What is the complexity of adding an element to the heap.
mcqs.explanation: The total possible operation in re locating the new location to a new element will be equal to height of the heap.

mcqs.question: The worst case complexity of deleting any arbitrary node value element from heap is __________
mcqs.explanation: The total possible operation in deleting the existing node and re locating new position to all its connected nodes will be equal to height of the heap.

mcqs.question: Heap can be used as ________________
mcqs.explanation: The property of heap that the value of root must be either greater or less than both of its children makes it work like a priority queue.

mcqs.question: If we implement heap as min-heap, deleting root node (value 1)from the heap. What would be the value of root node after second iteration if leaf node (value 100) is chosen to replace the root at start.
mcqs.explanation: As the root is deleted and node with value 100 is used as replaced one. There is a violation of property that root node must have value less than its children. So there will be shuffling of node with value 100 with node of value 2. And thus 2 becomes root. And it will remain to be at root after all the possible operations. So the value at root will be 2.

mcqs.question: If we implement heap as maximum heap , adding a new node of value 15 to the left most node of right subtree. What value will be at leaf nodes of the right subtree of the heap.
mcqs.explanation: As 15 is less than 25 so there would be no violation and the node will remain at that position. So leaf nodes with value 15 and 1 will be at the position in right sub tree.

mcqs.question: An array consists of n elements. We want to create a heap using the elements. The time complexity of building a heap will be in order of
mcqs.explanation: The total time taken will be N times the complexity of adding a single element to the heap. And adding a single element takes logN time, so That is equal to N*logN.

mcqs.question: What is the space complexity of searching in a heap?
mcqs.explanation: The space complexity of searching an element in heap is O (n). Heap consists of n elements and we need to compare every element. Here no addition or deletion of elements takes place. Hence space complexity is O (n).

mcqs.question: What is the best case complexity in building a heap?
mcqs.explanation: The best case complexity occurs in bottom-up construction when we have a sortes array given.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “D-ary Heap”.

mcqs.question: d-heap is similar to that of a?
mcqs.explanation: A d-heap is similar to that of a binary heap except that binary heaps have two children and d-heaps have d children.

mcqs.question: d-heap is shallower than a binary heap.
mcqs.explanation: d-heap is much shallower than a binary heap with respect to performance efficiency of insert and delete operations.

mcqs.question: Which operation cannot be directly performed in a d-heap?
mcqs.explanation: Find operation in a d-heap cannot be performed as in other heaps. This is the main weakness of d-heap.

mcqs.question: Which operation is not efficiently performed in a d-heap?

mcqs.question: What is the run time efficiency of an insertion algorithm in d-heap?

mcqs.question: How many comparisons will occur while performing a delete-min operation?
mcqs.explanation: Since, the delete-min operation is more expensive and the heap is shallow, the minimum of d elements can be found using d-1 comparisons.

mcqs.question: How many basic operations can be performed in a d-heap?
mcqs.explanation: The two basic operations performed in a d-heap are insert and delete-min operations.

mcqs.question: What is the run time efficiency of delete-min operation?
mcqs.explanation: The run time efficiency of a delete-min algorithm using d-1 comparisons is mathematically found to be O(d log<sub>d</sub> N).

mcqs.question: How many secondary operations are performed in a d-heap?
mcqs.explanation: The other operations that can be performed in a d-heap are increasekey, decreasekey, buildheap and delete.

mcqs.question: On which data structure is a d-ary heap based?
mcqs.explanation: d-ary heap is a priority queue based data structure that is a generalization of binary heaps.

mcqs.question: What is the highest element of the given maximum ternary heap?

mcqs.question: What is the child of smallest element of the given minimum ternary heap?

mcqs.question: What are the siblings of smallest element of the given maximum ternary heap?

mcqs.question: What is the height of a given minimum ternary heap?
mcqs.explanation: Minimum ternary heap has the smallest element as its root node. The parent node is all either equal or less than children node in a minimum ternary heap. Height is the total length from the root node to the leaf node. So the height of the minimum ternary heap is 1.

mcqs.question: What is the ancestor of the leaf node in a given minimum ternary heap?
mcqs.explanation: Minimum ternary heap has the smallest element as its root node. The parent node is all either equal or less than children node in a minimum ternary heap. Ancestor is the node falling on the path from that node to the root node. So here ancestor of all leaf nodes is 1.

mcqs.question: Which property should ternary heap hold for execution?

mcqs.question: Should leaves in ternary heap be distributed from left to right.

mcqs.question: What is the process of building a ternary heap called?

mcqs.question: Which type of data structure is a ternary heap?
mcqs.explanation: Ternary heap is a type of data structure in the field of computer science. It is a part of the Heap data structure family. It is a priority queue type of data structure that follows all the property of heap.

mcqs.question: Is the priority queue abstract data type.
mcqs.explanation: Priority queue is an abstract data type. It is also the extension of the Queue data structure where all the elements have been assigned some priority and on the basis of this priority, the elements are dequeued from the structure.

mcqs.question: What is a ternary heap?

options.a: a) An array with three elements
options.b: b) Linked list with three elements

mcqs.question: Who invented d-ary heap?
mcqs.explanation: Ternary heap is a type of data structure in the field of computer science. It is a part of the Heap data structure family. The d-ary heap was invented by Donald Johnson in the year 1975.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for inserting a new item in a ternary heap of n elements?
mcqs.explanation: In order to insert a new item in a ternary heap data structure having n elements, the heap has great efficiency for inserting them. So the time complexity for worst case is found to be O (log n/ log 3).

mcqs.question: Is decrease priority operation performed more quickly in a ternary heap with respect to the binary heap.
mcqs.explanation: Ternary heap is a type of data structure in the field of computer science. It is a part of the Heap data structure family. Due to the swapping process, the decrease priority operation performs more quickly in a ternary heap.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for decreasing priority of key in a minimum ternary heap of n elements?
mcqs.explanation: In order to decrease the priority of an item in a ternary heap data structure having n elements, the heap has great efficiency for decreasing them. So the time complexity for worst case is found to be O (log n/ log 3). This is due to the upwards swapping process.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for increasing priority of key in a maximum ternary heap of n elements?
mcqs.explanation: In order to increase the priority of an item in a ternary heap data structure having n elements, it performs upwards swapping. So the time complexity for worst case is found to be O (log n/ log 3).

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for deleting root key in a ternary heap of n elements?
mcqs.explanation: In order to delete a root key in a ternary heap data structure having n elements, it performs downward swapping. So the time complexity for worst case is found to be O (3log n/ log 3).

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for increasing priority of key in a minimum ternary heap of n elements?
mcqs.explanation: In order to the increasing the priority of key in a minimum ternary heap data structure having n elements, it performs downward swapping. So the time complexity for worst case is found to be O (3log n/ log 3).

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for decreasing priority of key in a maximum ternary heap of n elements?
mcqs.explanation: In order to decrease the priority of key in a maximum ternary heap data structure having n elements, it performs downward swapping. So the time complexity for worst case is found to be O (3log n/ log 3).

mcqs.question: Do ternary heap have better memory cache behavior than binary heap.
mcqs.explanation: Ternary heap is a type of data structure in the field of computer science. It is a part of the Heap data structure family. Due to the swapping process, they have better memory cache behavior.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity for creating a ternary heap using swapping?
mcqs.explanation: Ternary Heap can be formed by two swapping operations. Therefore, the time complexity for creating a ternary heap using two swapping operation is found to be O (n).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the application of minimum ternary heap?
mcqs.explanation: When working on the graph in the computer science field, the Prim’s Algorithm for spanning trees uses a minimum ternary heap as there are delete operation equal to a number of edges and decrease priority operation equal to the number of vertices associated with the graph.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Pairing Heap”.

mcqs.question: What is the reason for the efficiency of a pairing heap?
mcqs.explanation: The reason for the simplicity of a pairing heap is its simplicity as it is simpler and outperform other heap structures.

mcqs.question: How is a pairing heap represented?
mcqs.explanation: A pairing heap is represented as a heap-ordered tree and the analysis of pairing heap is open.

mcqs.question: The actual pairing heap implementation uses the right child and left child representation.
mcqs.explanation: The actual pairing heap implementation uses a left child and right sibling representation since it follows heap order property.

mcqs.question: Which node contains a pointer to its parent?
mcqs.explanation: A node that is a leftmost node contains a pointer to its parent, otherwise, the node is a right sibling.

mcqs.question: Which of the heaps is implemented by the following figure?
mcqs.explanation: The above figure is a representation of a pairing heap because it has left children and right siblings.

mcqs.question: What is the basic operation performed in a pairing heap?
mcqs.explanation: The basic operation performed in a pairing heap is merging. Insertion is also done by merging.

mcqs.question: If there are c children of the root, how many calls to the merge procedure is required to reassemble the heap?
mcqs.explanation: If there are c children of the root, then c-1 merges are required to reassemble the pairing heap.

mcqs.question: Which of the following methods is the best choice for complex applications?
mcqs.explanation: Pairing heap is the best choice for complex applications because it is simple and better than the others.

mcqs.question: Pairing heaps time complexity was inspired by that of?
mcqs.explanation: The pairing heaps insertion, deletion and search time complexity was initially inspired by that of splay trees.

mcqs.question: The roots of the elements of the subtrees are smaller than the root of the heap.
mcqs.explanation: The heap ordering property requires that all the root elements of the subtrees in the list are not smaller than the root element of the heap.

mcqs.question: The amortized time efficiency for performing deletion of a minimum element is?
mcqs.explanation: The amortized time efficiency for performing deletion of a minimum element is mathematically found to be O(log N).

mcqs.question: Out of the following given options, which is the fastest algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: Although pairing heap is an efficient algorithm, it is worse than the Fibonacci heap. Also, pairing heap is faster than d-ary heap and binary heap.

mcqs.question: What is the run time efficiency of an insertion algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: The run time efficiency of an insertion algorithm in a pairing heap is mathematically found to be O(N).

mcqs.question: Pointer manipulation is generally more time-consuming than multiplication and division.
mcqs.explanation: Use of pointers for merging reduces the speed of other operations. This is the main drawback of all advanced data structures.

mcqs.question: How many properties does a leftist heap support?
mcqs.explanation: A leftist heap supports two properties- structural property, ordering property and a heap order property.

mcqs.question: In a leftist heap, the null path length of a null node is defined as?
mcqs.explanation: In a leftist heap tree, the null path length of a null node with no children is defined as -1.

mcqs.question: How many nodes does a leftist tree with r nodes must have?
mcqs.explanation: A leftist tree with r nodes on the right path is proved to have at least 2<sup>r</sup>-1 nodes. This theorem is proved by induction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following operations does not destroy the leftist heap property?
mcqs.explanation: Performing insert and merge operations on the right path could destroy the leftist heap property. It is extremely easy to restore that property.

mcqs.question: What is the fundamental operation on leftist heap?
mcqs.explanation: The fundamental operations on leftist heaps is merge. Insertion operation is a merge of a one-node heap with a larger heap.

mcqs.question: A leftist heap is also said to be a binary heap.
mcqs.explanation: A leftist heap has a structural property and an ordering property which is similar to that of a binary heap. Hence, leftist heap is also said to be binary heap.

mcqs.question: What is the efficiency of merge used in leftist heaps?
mcqs.explanation: The efficiency of merge operations in leftist heap is mathematically found to be O( log N) which is the same in binary heaps.

mcqs.question: What is the node path length of a node with 0 or 1 child?
mcqs.explanation: The length of the shortest path from a node to a node without two children is defined as 0.

mcqs.question: Why is this heap named leftist heap?

options.b: b) the tree is biased to get deep down the left

mcqs.answer: b) the tree is biased to get deep down the left
mcqs.explanation: The heap is named as leftist heap because it tends to have deep left paths. It follows that the right path ought to be short.

mcqs.question: In a leftist heap, all the operations should be performed on?
mcqs.explanation: All the operations are performed on the right path because right paths are short. However, insertion and merges cannot be performed on the right path.

mcqs.question: What would be the result if the left subtree of the root has a null path length of 1 and the right subtree has a null path length of 2?
mcqs.explanation: When two leftist heaps are merged, if the left subtree of the root has a null path length of 1 and the right subtree has a null path length of 2, leftist property is violated at the root.

mcqs.question: What happens if the null path length is not updated?

options.b: b) all null path lengths will be 0
options.c: c) all null path lengths will be -1
options.d: d) all null path lengths will be 1

mcqs.answer: b) all null path lengths will be 0
mcqs.explanation: While performing insertion via merge operation in a leftist heap, if the null path length is not updated, all null path lengths will be 0.

mcqs.question: What is the time taken to delete a minimum element in a leftist heap?
mcqs.explanation: The time taken to delete a minimum element in a leftist heap is mathematically found to be O(log N).

mcqs.question: In what time can a leftist heap be built?
mcqs.explanation: The mathematical calculation yields a result that, a leftist heap can be built in O(N) time by building a binary heap.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Skew Heap”.

mcqs.question: ___________ is a self-adjusting version of a leftist heap.
mcqs.explanation: A skew heap is a self-adjusting version of a leftist heap and it is simpler to implement.

mcqs.question: The worst case running time of all operations in a skew heap is given as?
mcqs.explanation: The worst case running time of all operations in a skew heap is mathematically found to be O(N).

mcqs.question: What is the amortized cost per operation of a skew heap?
mcqs.explanation: The amortized cost per operation of a skew heap is O(log N) since the worst case analysis of skew heap is O(N) and splay tree is O(M log N).

mcqs.question: The relationship of skew heaps to leftist heaps is analogous to that of?

options.a: a) Splay tree and AVL tree
options.b: b) Red black tree and AVL tree
options.c: c) Binary tree and Splay tree
options.d: d) Binary tree and Red black tree

mcqs.answer: a) Splay tree and AVL tree
mcqs.explanation: Splay tree is a self -adjusting version of AVL tree. Similarly, skew heap is a self-adjusting version of leftist heap.

mcqs.question: What is the fundamental operation performed in skew heaps?
mcqs.explanation: The fundamental operation of skew heaps is merging. Hence, it is similar to that of a leftist heap.

mcqs.question: What is the time per operation of merging, insertion and deletion operations in a skew heap?
mcqs.explanation: Skew heaps support merging, insertion and deletion all effectively in O(log N) time per operation.

mcqs.question: Why would a recursive implementation fail in skew heaps?

options.a: a) skew heaps are self adjusting

mcqs.explanation: In skew heaps, a recursive implementation could fail because of lack of stack space even though performance is acceptable.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is difficult to determine the right path length?
mcqs.explanation: It is an open problem to determine precisely the expected right path length of both leftist and skew heaps and comparatively, the latter is difficult.

mcqs.question: The worst case analysis for a naïve merge is given as?
mcqs.explanation: The worst-case analysis for the naïve merge is an insertion in a right heavy tree. So, insertion takes O(N).

mcqs.question: How many types of the merge are available in skew heaps?
mcqs.explanation: Two kinds of the merge are available in skew heaps- naïve merge and skew merge.

mcqs.question: Naïve merge cannot be done in a skew merge.
mcqs.explanation: One way of doing skew merge is to begin with naïve merge and then swapping the left and right children of the tree.

mcqs.question: What is the amortized efficiency of skew merge?
mcqs.explanation: The amortized efficiency of a skew heap is mathematically found to be O( log N).

mcqs.question: In skew heaps, certain constraints are to be met in order to perform swapping.
mcqs.explanation: In skew heaps, swaps are unconditional. It is done with the exception that the largest of all nodes does not have its children swapped.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Min/Max Heap”.

mcqs.question: Descending priority queue can be implemented using ______
mcqs.explanation: Descending priority queue arranges the elements based on their priority or value and allows removing the elements in descending order. So, it can be efficiently implemented using max heap.

mcqs.question: Min heap can be used to implement selection sort.
mcqs.explanation: In min heap, the insertion and deletion operation takes O(logn) time. Therefore, a selection sort with n insertions and n deletions can be implemented using a min heap in O(nlogn) operations.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the valid min heap?

options.a: a)
options.b: b)
options.c: c)
options.d: d)

mcqs.answer: d)
mcqs.explanation: In min heap the smallest is located at the root and the largest elements are located at the leaf nodes. So, all leaf nodes need to be checked to find the largest element.

mcqs.question: The ascending heap property is ___________
mcqs.explanation: The min heap is also known as ascending heap. Min heap of size n is an almost complete binary tree of n nodes such that the element at each node is greater than or equal to the element at its parent node.

mcqs.question: The procedure FindMin() to find the minimum element and the procedure DeleteMin() to delete the minimum element in min heap take _________

options.a: a) logarithmic and linear time constant respectively
options.b: b) constant and linear time respectively
options.c: c) constant and quadratic time respectively
options.d: d) constant and logarithmic time respectively

mcqs.answer: d) constant and logarithmic time respectively
mcqs.explanation: In the min heap, the root is the maximum element in the tree. So, locating it takes constant time, but deleting it takes logarithmic time. Because after deleting it, the root is replaced with last element and then the procedure to maintain the min ordering is invoked.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following array elements represents a binary min heap?
mcqs.explanation: A tree is min heap when data at every node in the tree is smaller than or equal to it’s children’ s data. So, only 8 10 12 25 14 17 generates required tree.

mcqs.question: In a binary min heap containing n elements, the largest element can be found in __________ time.
mcqs.explanation: In min heap the smallest is located at the root and the largest elements are located at the leaf nodes. So, all leaf nodes need to be checked to find the largest element. Thus, worst case time will be O (n).

mcqs.question: Min heap is a complete binary tree.
mcqs.explanation: A tree, in which all levels are fully filled, except possibly the last level, is called as the complete binary tree. And min heap maintains shape property, so it is a complete binary tree. The shape property ensures that all levels in the min heap are fully filled, except the last one, and, if the last level is not filled completely, then fill the elements from left to right.

mcqs.question: What will be the position of 5, when a max heap is constructed on the input elements 5, 70, 45, 7, 12, 15, 13, 65, 30, 25?

options.b: b) 5 will be at last level
options.c: c) 5 will be at second level
options.d: d) 5 can be anywhere in heap

mcqs.answer: b) 5 will be at last level
mcqs.explanation: In max heap the greatest element is at the root and the smallest elements are at the last level. As 5 is the smallest input element, it will be at the last level.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Trie”.

mcqs.question: Trie is also known as _________
mcqs.explanation: Trie is a very useful data structure which is based on the prefix of a string. Trie is used to represent the “Retrieval” of data and thus the name Trie. And it is also known as a digital tree.

mcqs.question: What traversal over trie gives the lexicographical sorting of the set of the strings?
mcqs.explanation: In trie, we store the strings in such a way that there is one node for every common prefix. Therefore the inorder traversal over trie gives the lexicographically sorted set of strings.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the efficient data structure for searching words in dictionaries?
mcqs.explanation: In a BST, as well as in a balanced BST searching takes time in order of mlogn, where m is the maximum string length and n is the number of strings in tree. But searching in trie will take O(m) time to search the key.

mcqs.question: Which of the following special type of trie is used for fast searching of the full texts?
mcqs.explanation: Suffix tree, a special type of trie, contains all the suffixes of the given text at the key and their position in the text as their values. So, suffix trees are used for fast searching of the full texts.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not true?

options.a: a) Trie requires less storage space than hashing
options.b: b) Trie allows listing of all the words with same prefix
options.d: d) Trie is also known as prefix tree

mcqs.answer: a) Trie requires less storage space than hashing
mcqs.explanation: Both the hashing and the trie provides searching in the linear time. But trie requires extra space for storage and it is collision free. And trie allows finding all the strings with same prefix, so it is also called prefix tree.

mcqs.question: A program to search a contact from phone directory can be implemented efficiently using ______
mcqs.explanation: Dictionaries, phone directories can be implemented efficiently using the trie. Because it trie provides the efficient linear time searching over the entries.

mcqs.question: What can be the maximum depth of the trie with n strings and m as the maximum sting the length?
mcqs.explanation: In the trie, the strings are stored efficiently based on the common prefixes. And trie has maximum fan-out 26 if english alphabets are considered. Owing to this, the maximum depth is equal to the maximum string length.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is true about the trie?

options.b: b) path from root to the leat yields the string
options.c: c) children of nodes are randomly ordered
options.d: d) each node stores the associated keys

mcqs.answer: b) path from root to the leat yields the string
mcqs.explanation: A trie is an ordered tree where (i) the root represents an empty string(“”) (ii) each node other than root is labeled with a character (iii) the children of a nodes are lexicographically ordered (iv) the paths from the leaves to the root yields the strings.

mcqs.question: Auto complete and spell checkers can be implemented efficiently using the trie.
mcqs.explanation: Trie provides fast searching and storing of the words. And tries stores words in lexicographical order so, trie is the efficient data structure for implementation of spell checkers and auto complete.

mcqs.question: What is the other name for Suffix Tree?
mcqs.explanation: In computer science, a suffix tree is also known as PAT tree or position tree. It is a compressed search tree or prefix tree in which keys contain the suffix of text values as the text position.

mcqs.question: Which tree allows fast implementation of string operation?
mcqs.explanation: In computer science, a suffix tree is also known as PAT tree or position tree. It is a compressed search tree or prefix tree in which keys contain the suffix of text values as the text position. It allows fast string operation to be carried out by the user.

mcqs.question: How much time does construction of suffix tree take?

options.c: c) Exponential to Length of Tree
options.d: d) Linear to Length of Tree

mcqs.answer: d) Linear to Length of Tree
mcqs.explanation: Suffix tree is also known as PAT tree or position tree. It is a compressed search tree or prefix tree in which keys contain the suffix of text values as the text position. It allows fast string operation. Total time taken for construction of suffix tree is linear to the length of the tree.

mcqs.question: How much space does construction of suffix tree takes?

options.b: b) Exponential to Length of Tree
options.d: d) Linear to Length of Tree

mcqs.answer: d) Linear to Length of Tree
mcqs.explanation: Suffix tree is also known as PAT tree or position tree. It is a compressed search tree or prefix tree in which keys contain the suffix of text values as the text position. It allows fast string operation. Total space taken for construction of a suffix tree is linear to the length of the tree.

mcqs.question: Which tree provides a linear time solution for substring operation?
mcqs.explanation: It is a compressed search tree or prefix tree in which keys contain the suffix of text values as the text position. It allows fast string operation to be carried out by the user. The substring operation can be performed by suffix tree in linear time.

mcqs.question: Who proposed the concept of Suffix Tree?
mcqs.explanation: In computer science, a suffix tree is also known as PAT tree or position tree. It is a compressed search tree or prefix tree in which keys contain the suffix of text values as the text position. The concept of Suffix Tree was introduced by Weiner in 1973.

mcqs.question: Who among the following provided the first online contribution of Suffix Tree?

title: 10. Data Structure MCQ on Hash Tables

links.context: This set of Data Structure Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Hash Tables”.

mcqs.question: What is a hash table?

options.a: a) A structure that maps values to keys
options.b: b) A structure that maps keys to values
options.c: c) A structure used for storage
options.d: d) A structure used to implement stack and queue

mcqs.answer: b) A structure that maps keys to values
mcqs.explanation: A hash table is used to implement associative arrays which has a key-value pair, so the has table maps keys to values.

mcqs.question: If several elements are competing for the same bucket in the hash table, what is it called?
mcqs.explanation: In a hash table, if sevaral elements are computing for the same bucket then there will be a clash among elements. This condition is called Collision. The Collision is reduced by adding elements to a linked list and head address of linked list is placed in hash table.

mcqs.question: What is direct addressing?

options.a: a) Distinct array position for every possible key
options.b: b) Fewer array positions than keys
options.c: c) Fewer keys than array positions
options.d: d) Same array position for all keys

mcqs.answer: a) Distinct array position for every possible key
mcqs.explanation: Direct addressing is possible only when we can afford to allocate an array that has one position for every possible key.

mcqs.question: What is the search complexity in direct addressing?
mcqs.explanation: Since every key has a unique array position, searching takes a constant time.

mcqs.question: What is a hash function?

options.a: a) A function has allocated memory to keys
options.b: b) A function that computes the location of the key in the array
options.c: c) A function that creates an array
options.d: d) A function that computes the location of the values in the array

mcqs.answer: b) A function that computes the location of the key in the array
mcqs.explanation: In a hash table, there are fewer array positions than the keys, so the position of the key in the array has to be computed, this is done using the hash function.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a technique to avoid a collision?

options.a: a) Make the hash function appear random

mcqs.explanation: On increasing hash table size, space complexity will increase as we need to reallocate the memory size of hash table for every collision. It is not the best technique to avoid a collision. We can avoid collision by making hash function random, chaining method and uniform hashing.

mcqs.question: What is the load factor?
mcqs.explanation: In simple chaining, load factor is the average number of elements stored in a chain, and is given by the ratio of number of elements stored to the number of slots in the array.

mcqs.question: What is simple uniform hashing?

options.a: a) Every element has equal probability of hashing into any of the slots
options.b: b) A weighted probabilistic method is used to hash elements into the slots
options.c: c) Elements has Random probability of hashing into array slots
options.d: d) Elements are hashed based on priority

mcqs.answer: a) Every element has equal probability of hashing into any of the slots
mcqs.explanation: In simple uniform hashing, any given element is equally likely to hash into any of the slots available in the array.

mcqs.question: In simple uniform hashing, what is the search complexity?
mcqs.explanation: There are two cases, once when the search is successful and when it is unsuccessful, but in both the cases, the complexity is O(1+alpha) where 1 is to compute the hash function and alpha is the load factor.

mcqs.question: In simple chaining, what data structure is appropriate?
mcqs.explanation: Deletion becomes easier with doubly linked list, hence it is appropriate.

mcqs.question: The case in which a key other than the desired one is kept at the identified location is called?
mcqs.explanation: When some other value is placed at a specified location other than the desired key, it is said to be a collision.

mcqs.question: What data organization method is used in hash tables?
mcqs.explanation: The data structure used to organize data for hash tables is linked list. It contains a data field and a pointer field.

mcqs.question: The task of generating alternative indices for a node is called?
mcqs.explanation: Collision handling involves the process of formulating alternative indices for a key.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a collision resolution technique?
mcqs.explanation: Hashing is a technique of placing data items in specific locations. Collision may occur in hashing but hashing is not a collision resolution technique.

mcqs.question: Hashing is the problem of finding an appropriate mapping of keys into addresses.
mcqs.explanation: Hashing is a data structure which is used to locate data in a table based on a key value.

mcqs.question: In a hash table of size 10, where is element 7 placed?
mcqs.explanation:
The hash location is defined as hash(f)= key mod table_size.
7 mod 10 gives 7. It is placed in 7th position.

mcqs.question: What should be the load factor for separate chaining hashing?
mcqs.explanation: For hashing using separate chaining method, the load factor should be maintained as 1. For open addressing method, it should not exceed 0.5.

mcqs.question: Which of the following operations are done in a hash table?
mcqs.explanation: Hash tables are used to implement Insert and Find operations in constant average time. This is the prime purpose of hashing.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is identical to that of a separate chaining hash node?
mcqs.explanation: The hash node in separate chaining is similar to that of a linked list. The separate chaining hash table is an array of linked lists.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the hashing function for separate chaining?
mcqs.explanation: The hashing function for separate chaining is given by H(x)= key mod table size. H(x)=hash(x)+i2  mod table size defines quadratic probing.

mcqs.question: What is the correct notation for a load factor?
mcqs.explanation: In general, load factor is denoted as ⅄. In separate chaining method, load factor is maintained as 1.0.

mcqs.question: In hash tables, how many traversal of links does a successful search require?
mcqs.explanation: A successful search requires about 1+ (⅄/2) links to be traversed. There is a guarantee that at least one link must be traversed.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of using separate chaining using linked lists?

options.d: d) It does not resolve collision

mcqs.explanation: One of the major disadvantages of using separate chaining is the requirement of pointers. If the number of elements are more, it requires more pointers.

mcqs.question: What is the worst case search time of a hashing using separate chaining algorithm?
mcqs.explanation: The worst case search time of separate chaining algorithm using linked lists is mathematically found to be O(N).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is used in hash tables to determine the index of any input record?
mcqs.explanation: Hash table is an example of a data structure that is built for fast access of elements. Hash functions are used to determine the index of any input record in a hash table.

mcqs.question: What is the advantage of a hash table as a data structure?

options.c: c) very efficient for less number of entries
options.d: d) exhibit good locality of reference

mcqs.explanation: Hash table is a data structure that has an advantage that it allows fast access of elements. Hash functions are used to determine the index of any input record in a hash table.

mcqs.question: What is the use of a hash function?

options.a: a) to calculate and return the index of corresponding data

mcqs.answer: a) to calculate and return the index of corresponding data
mcqs.explanation: Hash function calculates and returns the index for corresponding data. This data is then mapped in a hash table.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of insert function in a hash table using a doubly linked list?
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of insert function in a hash table is O(1). Condition is that the number of collisions should be low.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of search function in a hash table using a doubly linked list?
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of search function in a hash table is O(1). Condition is that the number of collisions should be low.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of delete function in the hash table using a doubly linked list?
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of delete function in a hash table is O(1). Condition is that the hash function should be such that the number of collisions should be low.

mcqs.question: Hashing can be used to encrypt and decrypt digital signatures.
mcqs.explanation: Hashing is also used in encryption algorithms. It is used for encryption and decryption of digital signatures.

mcqs.question: What is the advantage of using a doubly linked list for chaining over singly linked list?

options.b: b) it is easy to implement
options.c: c) it makes the process of insertion and deletion faster

mcqs.answer: c) it makes the process of insertion and deletion faster
mcqs.explanation: Using a doubly linked list reduces time complexity significantly. Though it uses more memory to store the extra pointer.

mcqs.question: Which of the following technique stores data in the hash table itself in case of a collision?

options.c: c) Chaining using doubly linked list

mcqs.explanation: Open addressing is used to store data in the table itself in case of a collision. Whereas chaining stores data in a separate entity.

mcqs.question: Which of the following technique stores data in a separate entity in case of a collision?

options.b: b) Chaining using doubly linked list

mcqs.answer: b) Chaining using doubly linked list
mcqs.explanation: Chaining using doubly linked list is used to store data in a separate entity (doubly linked list in this case) in case of a collision. Whereas open addressing stores it in the table itself.

mcqs.question: Collision is caused due to the presence of two keys having the same value.
mcqs.explanation: A collision is caused due to the presence of two keys having the same value. It is handled by using any one of the two methods namely:- Chaining and Open addressing.

mcqs.question: Which of the following variant of a hash table has the best cache performance?

options.a: a) hash table using a linked list for separate chaining
options.b: b) hash table using binary search tree for separate chaining
options.c: c) hash table using open addressing
options.d: d) hash table using a doubly linked list for separate chaining

mcqs.answer: c) hash table using open addressing
mcqs.explanation: Implementation of the hash table using open addressing has a better cache performance as compared to separate chaining. It is because open addressing stores data in the same table without using any extra space.

mcqs.question: What is the advantage of hashing with chaining?

options.c: c) less sensitive to hash function
options.d: d) has a time complexity of O(n) in the worst case

mcqs.answer: c) less sensitive to hash function
mcqs.explanation: Hashing with separate chaining has an advantage that it is less sensitive to a hash function. It is also easy to implement.

mcqs.question: What is the disadvantage of hashing with chaining?

options.c: c) quite sensitive to hash function
options.d: d) table gets filled up easily

mcqs.explanation: Hashing with separate chaining has a disadvantage that it takes more space. This space is used for storing elements in case of a collision.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of insert function in a hash table using a binary tree?
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of insert function in a hash table is O(1) on an average. Condition is that the number of collisions should be low.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of the search function in a hash table using a binary tree?
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of search function in a hash table is O(1). Condition is that the number of collisions should be low.

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of the delete function in the hash table using a binary tree?
mcqs.explanation: Time complexity of delete function in a hash table is O(1). Condition is that the hash function should be such that the number of collisions should be low.

mcqs.question: What is the advantage of a hash table over BST?

options.a: a) hash table has a better average time complexity for performing insert, delete and search operations
options.b: b) hash table requires less space
options.c: c) range query is easy with hash table

mcqs.answer: a) hash table has a better average time complexity for performing insert, delete and search operations
mcqs.explanation: Hash table and BST both are examples of data structures. Hash table has an advantage that it has a better time complexity for performing insert, delete and search operations.

mcqs.question: What is the disadvantage of BST over the hash table?

options.a: a) BST is easier to implement
options.b: b) BST can get the keys sorted by just performing inorder traversal
options.c: c) BST can perform range query easily
options.d: d) Time complexity of hash table in inserting, searching and deleting is less than that of BST

mcqs.answer: d) Time complexity of hash table in inserting, searching and deleting is less than that of BST
mcqs.explanation: BST has an advantage that it is easier to implement, can get the keys sorted by just performing in-order traversal and can perform range query easily. Hash table has lesser time complexity for performing insert, delete and search operations.

mcqs.question: Which of the following technique stores data separately in case of a collision?

options.d: d) Chaining using a binary tree

mcqs.answer: d) Chaining using a binary tree
mcqs.explanation: Open addressing is used to store data in the table itself in case of a collision. Whereas chaining stores data in a separate entity.

mcqs.question: Separate chaining is easier to implement as compared to open addressing.
mcqs.explanation: There are two methods of handling collisions in a hash table:- open addressing and separate chaining. Open addressing requires more computation as compared to separate chaining.

mcqs.question: In open addressing the hash table can never become full.
mcqs.explanation: There are two methods of handling collisions in a hash table:- open addressing and separate chaining. In open addressing the hash table can become full.

mcqs.question: Which of the following trait of a hash function is most desirable?

options.a: a) it should cause less collisions
options.b: b) it should cause more collisions

mcqs.question: What is the time complexity of insert function in a hash table using list head?

mcqs.question: What is the advantage of using linked list over the doubly linked list for chaining?

mcqs.question: What is the worst case time complexity of insert function in the hash table when the list head is used for chaining?

mcqs.question: Which of the following technique is used for handling collisions in a hash table?

mcqs.question: By implementing separate chaining using list head we can reduce the number of collisions drastically.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an advantage of open addressing over separate chaining?

mcqs.question: Which of the following schemes does quadratic probing come under?
mcqs.explanation: Quadratic probing comes under open addressing scheme to resolve collisions in hash tables.

mcqs.question: Quadratic probing overcomes primary collision.
mcqs.explanation: Quadratic probing can overcome primary collision that occurs in linear probing but a secondary collision occurs in quadratic probing.

mcqs.question: What kind of deletion is implemented by hashing using open addressing?
mcqs.explanation: Standard deletion cannot be performed in an open addressing hash table, because the cells might have caused collision. Hence, the hash tables implement lazy deletion.

mcqs.question: In quadratic probing, if the table size is prime, a new element cannot be inserted if the table is half full.
mcqs.explanation: In quadratic probing, if the table size is prime, we can insert a new element even though table is exactly half filled. We can’t insert element if table size is more than half filled.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct function definition for quadratic probing?
mcqs.explanation: The function of quadratic probing is defined as F(i)=i<sup>2</sup>. The function of linear probing is defined as F(i)=i.

mcqs.question: How many constraints are to be met to successfully implement quadratic probing?
mcqs.explanation: 2 requirements are to be met with respect to table size. The table size should be a prime number and the table size should not be more than half full.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is the best technique to handle collision?
mcqs.explanation: Quadratic probing handles primary collision occurring in the linear probing method. Although secondary collision occurs in quadratic probing, it can be removed by extra multiplications and divisions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following techniques offer better cache performance?
mcqs.explanation: Linear probing offers better cache performance than quadratic probing and also it preserves locality of reference.

mcqs.question: What is the formula used in quadratic probing?

options.a: a) Hash key = key mod table size
options.b: b) Hash key=(hash(x)+F(i)) mod table size
options.c: c) Hash key=(hash(x)+F(i<sup>2</sup>)) mod table size

mcqs.answer: c) Hash key=(hash(x)+F(i<sup>2</sup>)) mod table size
mcqs.explanation: Hash key=(hash(x)+F(i<sup>2</sup>)) mod table size is the formula for quadratic probing. Hash key = (hash(x)+F(i)) mod table size is the formula for linear probing.

links.context: This set of Data Structures & Algorithms Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Hashing Functions”.

mcqs.question: Which scheme uses a randomization approach?
mcqs.explanation: Universal hashing scheme uses a randomization approach whereas hashing by division and hashing by multiplication are heuristic in nature.

mcqs.question: Which hash function satisfies the condition of simple uniform hashing?
mcqs.explanation:
If the keys are known to be random real numbers k independently and uniformly distributed in the range 0<=k<=1, the hash function which satisfies the condition of simple uniform hashing is
h(k)= lowerbound(km).

mcqs.question: A good hash approach is to derive the hash value that is expected to be dependent of any patterns that might exist in the data.
mcqs.explanation: A hash value is expected to be unrelated or independent of any patterns in the distribution of keys.

mcqs.question:
Interpret the given character string as an integer expressed in suitable radix notation. 
Character string = pt
mcqs.explanation: The given character string can be interpreted as (112,116) (Ascii values) then expressed as a radix-128 integer, hence the value is 112*128 + 116 = 14452.

mcqs.question: What is the hash function used in the division method?
mcqs.explanation: In division method for creating hash functions,  k keys are mapped into one of m slots by taking the reminder of k divided by m.

mcqs.question: What can be the value of m in the division method?
mcqs.explanation: A prime number not too close to an exact power of 2 is often a good choice for m since it reduces the number of collisions which are likely to occur.

mcqs.question: Which scheme provides good performance?
mcqs.explanation: Universal hashing scheme provides better performance than other schemes because it uses a unique randomisation approach.

mcqs.question: Using division method, in a given hash table of size 157, the key of value 172 be placed at position ____
mcqs.explanation:
The key 172 can be placed at position 15 by using the formula
